stillOpen.how: keel show open-issues . | open_issues intersected with the pending set

rows.title: Bulk-delete guard only fired at exactly-empty; a partial manifest shrink deleted the missing files
rows.description: DI-1: guardBulkDelete = remote.size===0 only, so a partial index (restore/reindex over an incomplete dir) advertising some files and dropping others propagated real delete-local on every device. Fixed: ratio guard (>= half of base missing from a non-empty manifest, min 6).

rows.title: Cached chunks bypassed DI-2 verification, laundering server bit-rot into a streamed file
rows.description: DI-R2#1 (HIGH): fetchFileBytes cached chunks unverified and streamFileToDisk verified only on a cache MISS, so a corrupt blob cached during an aborted buffered fetch was trusted on a later dedup cache hit and re-pushed as canonical corruption. Fixed: getVerifiedChunk verifies before caching in both paths. +test.

rows.title: Server seeds a publicly-known admin/admin account by default
rows.description: SEC-2: SYNC_USER/SYNC_PASSWORD default to admin/admin, seeding the server-admin account; an exposed default server is trivially taken over. Fix (coded, cargo-green): refuse to start when the admin password is unset/'admin' unless ALLOW_WEAK_ADMIN=1 (LAN/dev opt-in). Needs operator redeploy.

rows.title: Downloaded file content was never re-hashed; a corrupt chunk was laundered into known-good state
rows.description: DI-2: applyPull set base = claimed hash without verifying the reassembled bytes, so a bit-rotted blob was written to the note and re-served to every device. Fixed: verify sha256(bytes)==rmeta.hash; refuse + skip on mismatch.

rows.title: A re-queued edit was stranded on the idle-poll short-circuit under a green light
rows.description: CONC-R2#1 (HIGH): onRemoteChanged's idle short-circuit returned before the drainPending() call, so a path re-queued by the CONC#6 fix was never retried while syncDone flipped the light green over the unsynced edit. Fixed: drainPending runs in the finally on every path.

rows.title: Clean auto-merge fed stale localBytes into merge3, silently dropping a save that raced the fetch
rows.description: DI-R3#1 (MED-HIGH): the DI-R2#5 fix re-read current disk for the conflict-copy + read-only paths but NOT the clean-merge branch, which still merged base+STALE-local+remote and overwrote disk — losing keystrokes autosaved during the multi-chunk fetch, with no conflict copy. Fixed: re-read current disk (liveLocal) after the fetch and use it for the whole merge/conflict decision.

rows.title: A transient per-file error pinned the status light 'Offline' forever
rows.description: CO-2: the FSM cleared 'offline' only on 'connected', which the poll path never emits, so one failed edit left it red while sync kept working. Fixed: offline recovers to idle on a successful sync (syncDone).

rows.title: Fire-and-forget persist() fan-out raced, dropping a base entry (corrupted merge ancestor)
rows.description: CONC#1: reconcileAll fired void persist() per setBase, so N concurrent saveData writes to data.json could land out of order and an earlier snapshot overwrote a later one, losing a base entry. Fixed: single-flight coalescing writer — one write at a time, trailing write re-snapshots the latest state.

rows.title: A read-write share grantee can push plugin code the owner's device auto-loads (cross-share RCE)
rows.description: SEC-3: the server stores any committed path and the client auto-enables community-plugin code; a RW grantee committing .obsidian/plugins/x/main.js executes code on the owner's device. Fix: never auto-enable plugin code received over a shared (non-owned) vault; require explicit per-plugin confirmation.

rows.title: Both-absent left a stale base, so recreating a file with identical content deleted it
rows.description: CO-1: the in-sync handler never cleared base when both sides were absent, so a recreate with content equal to the old base hash read as delete-local and wiped the note. Fixed: clear stale base on both-absent.

rows.title: Streamed large-file downloads skipped the reassembly hash verification the buffered path enforces
rows.description: DI#2: streamFileToDisk appended chunks straight to disk and applyPull stamped base=claimed-hash without re-hashing, so on-disk server bit rot laundered into a known-good base and pushed back as canonical corruption. Fixed: verify each fetched chunk against its content address before writing (streaming-friendly; content-addressed ⇒ all-chunks-good ⇒ file good). +negative test.

rows.title: Vault switch bypassed the selective-sync accepts() gate, deleting another device's config on the server
rows.description: DI#1: switchTo iterated the RAW server manifest, so an 'upload' switch from a device filtering out a .obsidian category deleted every such file on the server (wiping another device's plugins/themes/settings), and a 'download' switch recorded a base for filtered paths (later misread as delete-remote). Fixed: switchTo filters the manifest through the same accepts() gate reconcileOne uses.

rows.title: Config-sync feature shipped unrooted, with zero requirement->test traceability
rows.description: The multi-device config divergence/removal defects (0.10.4: a crash on a divergent community-plugins.json + a phantom-base deletion of a peer's plugin) escaped a 125-test suite. Two-layer cause: (1) the config/customization-sync feature was implemented in code with NO Need or SystemRequirement behind it (an orphan capability), so there were no behavioral acceptance criteria and no use case enumerating the 'two already-configured devices' scenario; (2) tier-satisfaction showed SR-verified-by-Test at 0/15 — every automated test was divorced from the requirements model, so nothing enforced that a requirement carried a behavioral test. Tests were written bottom-up from the code (filter combos, single-file one-way config sync) and never exercised config conflict-copy or removal.

rows.title: Username case-collision on a case-insensitive FS gave cross-account vault access
rows.description: SEC#1: the user store keys case-sensitively but DATA_ROOT/<user>/<vault> collapses case on Windows/macOS, so 'Alice' and 'alice' were distinct accounts sharing one directory — one could read/write the other's vault (and 'ADMIN' vs 'admin' the admin's data). Fixed: safe_name is lowercase-canonical, so store-key == on-disk segment; no two names collide. +test.

rows.title: Session bearer token is passed in the WebSocket URL query string
rows.description: SEC-1: the 30-day token rides as ?token=... on the /api/ws upgrade, so it lands in reverse-proxy/LB logs and can be replayed. Fix: authenticate the WS via Sec-WebSocket-Protocol or a short-lived single-use ticket (coordinated client+server change).

rows.title: delete-local fired on a file's ABSENCE from the remote, not a real tombstone — wrong/empty server silently wiped the vault
rows.description: CRITICAL field data-loss: reconcile.decide() returned delete-local whenever a file present locally with an unchanged base was ABSENT from the remote (L!=null, R==null, L==B). Pointing a populated vault at a WRONG / FRESH / RESTORED server (a server that legitimately lacks our files but has issued NO deletion tombstones for them) therefore read every local file as a remote deletion and removed it. The one-shot C2 empty-server guard did not survive across reconcile passes — the client's own pushes made the remote non-empty on the second pass, disarming it — so even the '(server said it kept 2 local files)' log was immediately undone by the next reconcile (v1->v13). Fix: deletion is now TOMBSTONE-AUTHORITATIVE — reconcileOne takes a hasTombstone(path) predicate (reconcileAll from resp.deletes, reconcilePath from manifest.deletes); on absence WITHOUT a tombstone the file is RESTORED (pushed back), and it is removed ONLY when the server genuinely tombstoned it. Absence is never proof of deletion.

rows.title: The reconcile test suite CODIFIED the absence-delete bug and never covered a vault switch onto a wrong/empty server
rows.description: The 181-test suite missed the data-loss because the fake server modeled deletion as mere ABSENCE (files.delete with no tombstone), so tests could not distinguish a real deletion from a file the server never had — and TWO tests actively asserted the buggy delete-on-absence as correct behavior. Coverage was happy-path (deletion propagation) + a single-pass empty-server guard; nothing exercised the two-pass 'switch to a wrong/empty/restored server' sequence that reproduces in the field. Fix (the permanent guard, D0047): the fake server now models tombstones (deletions[] with versions; changes() returns them), the two mis-asserting tests were rewritten to correct tombstone semantics, and a DATA-LOSS REGRESSION test reproduces the exact field sequence (Welcome.md + 'test file.md' survive two reconciles against a wrong/empty server). Also hardened the orchestration seam: main.ts injection seams + an obsidian stub let plugin-wiring.test.ts cover the wiring, and the e2e harness was repaired (ALLOW_WEAK_ADMIN + createVault for protocol-6).

rows.title: A CAS 409 on the single-path event reconcile flaps the engine offline (regression from 0.10.26 CAS)
rows.description: CONC-R6#1 (HIGH): reconcileAll isolates a per-file CommitConflictError (skip -> merge next pass), but reconcilePath had no such guard, and the SyncEngine turns any thrown effect into failToOffline. So a routine same-file concurrent edit (the common desktop path) — which the 0.10.26 CAS work made 409 — dropped the client to offline + backoff, flapping on repeated edits. Fixed 0.10.27: reconcilePath isolates a CommitConflictError like reconcileAll (leave base unchanged -> next reconcile merges); any OTHER error still propagates -> offline.

rows.title: Corrupt-index reindex drops ALL tombstones, resurrecting deleted files (recovery path induces loss)
rows.description: RC-R7#1 (HIGH): a parse-corrupt index opens as Index::default() (empty deletions); reindex rebuilds files from disk but never restores tombstones (they existed only in the now-unparseable index), so changes(0) reports zero deletes and a long-offline client reads its since-deleted files as absence-without-tombstone -> RESTORES them (induced, user-perceived resurrection). The documented repair itself induces the resurrection Round 6 fixed for the cap case. Tombstones can't be reconstructed from disk, so the correct fix is the horizon + prompted-reconcile: a corrupt reindex IS a history reset. Folded into historyRebase.

rows.title: SEC-3 gate's owner-direction hole: a readWrite peer's plugin code auto-executes on the vault owner
rows.description: SEC-R6#1 (HIGH): the config-apply gate only suppressed auto-enable when vaultOwner was set (i.e. syncing a NON-owned vault). But a vault you OWN and share readWrite also holds an untrusted writer's content — a peer commits .obsidian/plugins/<id>/main.js and the owner's client auto-disables+enables the plugin, executing the peer's code (RCE, full Node access). The SEC-3 predicate was written too narrowly ('non-owned vault') vs the real one ('any vault with an untrusted writer'). Fixed 0.10.27: flushConfigReload never auto-enables synced plugin code for ANY vault — the user reloads manually. Refines STPA UCA-7 / SR-5.

rows.title: reindex aborts wholesale on one unrecoverable file -> permanent vault brick, shell-only escape
rows.description: RC-R7#2 (HIGH): the DI-4 'refuse to drop indexed-but-missing files' guard becomes a brick when a file is genuinely gone (mirror-write failed AND chunk lost) — every reindex (owner or admin) aborts, the vault stays ERROR forever, escapable only by hand-deleting files in a shell. Fixed 0.10.28: reindex RECOVERS a missing-from-disk file from the authoritative chunk store where its chunks survive (the common failed-mirror case, no data loss); only truly-lost files abort, and an admin force drops them so the rest is repaired.

rows.title: Arbitrary tombstone cap (MAX_TOMBSTONES) resurrects deleted files under tombstone-authoritative delete
rows.description: DI-R6#1 (HIGH): the server capped retained deletion tombstones at 10,000 on the pre-0.10.25 premise that 'a full reconcile infers deletion from absence' — a premise 0.10.25 INVERTED (absence -> restore, not delete). A long-offline client returning after >10k deletions finds the tombstone compacted away, reads the genuine deletion as 'server never had it', and RE-UPLOADS the file — resurrecting it fleet-wide (induced, user-perceived integrity violation, though not byte-loss). Two subsystems hardened in different rounds against opposite failure modes contradicted each other. Fixed 0.10.27: removed the arbitrary cap; tombstones are durable, so a genuine deletion is always distinguishable from a wrong/fresh server. The proper bound on growth is a deliberate history rebase (historyRebase), not an arbitrary count.

rows.title: IA.3.5.3 overstated MET — MFA not required for privileged accounts
rows.description: ASSESSOR-CRITICAL: MFA was purely opt-in self-enrollment; nothing required a privileged account to have it (totp_enabled consulted only at login; admin_grant had no MFA precondition; bootstrap admin is password-only), so the 'MET' claim overstated the control ('USE MFA FOR privileged accounts'). RESOLVED: added REQUIRE_ADMIN_MFA=1 — require_admin denies a privileged account until it enrolls TOTP (enrollment reachable while blocked, no lockout); posture reworded to an operator-configured control (like TLS). Class: overstated MET / authz.

rows.title: Authenticated memory-amplification DoS via concurrent large commits
rows.description: A single commit is bounded to req.size <= MAX_FILE_BYTES (512 MiB), but a client owning up to 100 vaults could fire many ~512 MiB reassemblies concurrently (each transient) and OOM a modest box. RESOLVED: large commits (req.size > 16 MiB) acquire a small global permit pool (MAX_CONCURRENT_LARGE_COMMITS=4) with a 30s bounded wait (503 on shed); small note commits are unthrottled — aggregate large-reassembly RAM is bounded. Class: availability.

rows.title: reconcileDelta doesn't supply locallyPresent → C1 guard inert on the poll-delta path
rows.description: KEYSTONE (found independently by the data-integrity AND sync critics, same reconcile.ts:396 citation): the incremental delta path called reconcileOne without locallyPresent, so the C1 'present-but-unreadable != deleted' guard was dead there. A momentarily-unreadable file (AV lock / unhydrated cloud placeholder) during a poll delta could be mis-decided as an unguarded delete-remote (wiping a fully-synced note fleet-wide) or cleared-then-resurrected. RESOLVED: reconcileDelta probes io.exists (defaulting to present) and passes locallyPresent, so the guard fires (skip + retry). Class: silent divergence / data loss.

rows.title: Admin A3: forced-change accounts bounce at login with no way in
rows.description: Login ignored must_change_password; an admin-created/reset account stored a token, then /api/admin/me 403'd and the UI silently returned to login with no message and no change-password control. RESOLVED: a forced-change screen (POST /api/password). Class: dead-end dialog path.

rows.title: Admin A1: Sign out doesn't revoke the server session
rows.description: Admin page 'Sign out' cleared only local sessionStorage; it never called POST /api/logout, so the bearer token stayed valid for its 30-day TTL. RESOLVED: signOut() now revokes server-side (best-effort). Class: discarded control effect.

rows.title: Plugin P1: setup wizard persists the plaintext password in token-only mode
rows.description: finish() wrote st.password unconditionally AND set authToken, so freshLogin (the only place that clears the password when !storePassword) never ran — the plaintext password lingered in data.json against the token-only-at-rest default. RESOLVED: wizardCredentials() (pure, unit-tested) only persists it when storePassword. Class: security side-effect.

rows.title: sameIgnoringEol / cosmeticEqual lossy-decode BINARY → two different attachments collapse to equal → silent local data loss
rows.description: Correctness critic (High). The cosmetic-EOL guard (reconcile.ts) and the modal auto-dismiss (noteconflict.ts) normalized via a NON-fatal TextDecoder, which maps every invalid byte to U+FFFD. Two genuinely different binary blobs whose differing bytes are both invalid UTF-8 normalize to the SAME string → the guard adopts remote over local with NO conflict copy (reconcile), or the modal auto-deletes this device's only copy — silent data loss for attachments, the exact 'never clobber on divergence' invariant the module protects. RESOLVED (1.0.31): both loci gate the cosmetic check on isMergeable(path,bytes) (extension- AND fatal-UTF-8-gated), so binary / invalid-UTF-8 content is excluded and can never be lossy-collapsed; genuine text keeps the false-EOL fix. Test: reconcile 'NO-BASE BINARY divergence keeps BOTH — never lossy-collapsed'. Class: data-integrity (silent clobber).

rows.title: Read-only shared vault manufactures unsyncable, permanently-flagged conflict copies for a no-base divergence (FIELD)
rows.description: FIELD-REPORTED: a read-only shared vault kept false-flagging conflicts. Root cause: reconcile's conflict-copy branch fired on read-only for a NO-COMMON-BASE divergence (decide()'s conservative default, not a real reader edit). A binary attachment (PNG) present on both the reader and the owner with differing bytes and no base → conflict-copy → the read-only branch wrote a local '(conflict …)' copy. On a read-only share that copy can NEVER push, so it's permanent litter: deriveNoteConflicts flags it forever AND it fires 'local change won't sync' every reconcile (the reported log line's path was the copy itself). RESOLVED (1.0.31): on read-only, only preserve a copy for a genuine both-sides edit against a KNOWN base (action 'merge'); a no-base divergence adopts the owner's bytes with NO copy. Also: the push case no longer reports an existing conflict-copy file as 'won't sync' (it's deliberately local). Class: false-positive conflict / read-only semantics.

rows.title: On mobile the only persistent status is a textless icon in the sidebar drawer with no reachable tooltip
rows.description: HF critique, High (gulf of evaluation / Nielsen #1). Mobile gets a ribbon icon only; the informative text lives in an aria-label (no touch tooltip) and the settings card — so 'did my note sync?' takes 2-3 taps on the platform whose goal is glanceable. PARTIALLY RESOLVED (1.6.0): added a 'Sync status' command that toasts the current status text (a one-tap words readout, works on mobile). NOTE: a truly persistent on-screen TEXT indicator isn't available — Obsidian mobile has no status bar and view.addAction is icon-only; the opt-in in-editor indicator (glanceable colour at the note) remains the persistent option. Class: status legibility (platform-limited; partially mitigated).

rows.title: Plugin adoption ends in an invisible restart requirement; a fresh vault's empty plugin list reads as 'nothing to sync'
rows.description: UX critique (all 3 lenses), HIGH. After 'Install all from the sync', the settings pane re-renders showing the plugins as synced, but nothing is active: files download on the next reconcile and Obsidian only loads plugins at STARTUP, so they stay dormant until a full restart — the only hint was a transient async toast saying 'reload Obsidian' (meaningless on mobile). Looks done, isn't → users re-tap or conclude it failed. Separately, on a fresh vault before the first reconcile reports server plugins, the checklist was EMPTY and read as 'nothing to sync' (the list populates minutes later). RESOLVED (1.4.0): a STANDING banner in the Synced-community-plugins group counts plugins adopted-but-not-installed-locally and says 'fully close and reopen Obsidian (on mobile, swipe the app away) to enable them'; and a 'Checking the server for plugins…' placeholder shows while the server list is still empty. Class: silent-until-later step / discoverability.

rows.title: Status indicator misleads: green 'Fully synced' on a read-only vault, and one yellow SPINNER covers healthy-polling + connecting + syncing
rows.description: HF critique, HIGH (gulf of evaluation / mode error / alarm habituation). (F1) On a read-only shared vault Obsidian still lets the user EDIT, but those edits never upload — yet statusDisplay's idle branch showed a plain green 'Fully synced', implying the user's changes are safe on the server (they're stranded or overwritten). (F3) idle-over-polling rendered the SAME yellow refresh-cw SPINNER as connecting/syncing, so a healthy device on a dropped websocket sat at a permanent spinner — indistinguishable from 'stuck', training panic or habituation. RESOLVED (1.5.1): idle on a read-only vault reads 'Synced (read-only) — your edits stay on this device' with a lock glyph; idle (realtime OR polling) now uses a STEADY glyph (check/lock), never the spinner — the spinner is reserved for the active connecting/syncing states; colour still distinguishes green vs yellow. Test: plugin-wiring statusDisplay read-only case. Class: status legibility / mode error.

rows.title: Irreversible actions (mirror-switch delete, fork-overwrite, sign-out) are less guarded than harmless ones
rows.description: UX critique (flows lens), HIGH. The plugin guarded SAFE actions but under-guarded IRREVERSIBLE ones: (1) the vault-switch 'Download'/'Upload' mirror modes DELETE local-only / remote-only files on a single warning-styled tap with no confirmation — while the non-destructive 'Leave share' has a full confirm(); (2) Fork uploads unconditionally (skips the switch resolve-prompt), so a fork name that already matches an owned vault would OVERWRITE it with no check; (3) 'Sign out' (token-only mode → no saved password) sits next to 'Change password' with no confirm, easy to fat-finger, and strands the user needing their password. RESOLVED (1.3.2): applySwitch confirm()s Download/Upload naming which side loses files ('can't be undone'); doFork refuses/confirms when the name already exists (checks the loaded vault list); Sign out confirm()s ('you'll need your password to sign back in; local files kept'). Merge (safe) still needs no confirm. Class: destructive-action guarding / data-safety.

rows.title: community-plugins.json synced as an opaque blob → a shorter synced copy DISABLES a locally-installed plugin
rows.description: community-plugins.json is the SET of enabled community-plugin ids (and gates whether installed plugins RUN), but config sync treated it as an opaque whole-file blob resolved by taking ONE whole side. So adopting a shorter synced copy (a pull where the remote dropped an id, or a divergence resolved to 'remote') would DISABLE every plugin not in that list — including SelfSync's own id — even though the plugin is installed+enabled locally. This is the DISABLE half of the 'all my plugins vanished' class (distinct from issueFalseAbsenceDelete's DELETE half). Surfaced while diagnosing the OneDrive field report, where the owner explicitly asked for proper behavior rather than a guard. FIX (correct-by-construction): community-plugins.json is now UNION-merged (isEnabledListConfig + mergeEnabledPluginsJson in configsync.ts; a dedicated branch in reconcileOne) — a grow-only set of enabled ids. A pull/divergence keeps every locally-enabled id and adds the remote's, and pushes the union so the server converges; a read-only share keeps the union locally. Enables propagate; a disable does not (toggled per device) — the catastrophe-proof asymmetry the owner chose. Verified: configsync.test (mergeEnabledPluginsJson union/empty/null), reconcile.test (fail-first: a shorter pull keeps the local plugin + converges the server; adopts a longer list), and a real-Obsidian two-device e2e (configsync.pwspec: A's plugin propagates to B, B's own plugin not disabled). Severity High (availability/data class). discoveredInField=false.

rows.title: delete-remote tombstoned on absence-from-the-LISTING, not CONFIRMED absence (cloud-placeholder / failed-enumeration data-loss vector)
rows.description: The batch reconcile path (reconcileAll/reconcileDelta) derived a file's local presence from io.list(), which UNDER-REPORTS when a directory fails to enumerate (ObsidianVaultIo.enumerateConfig swallowed the adapter.list error as an empty dir) or a cloud-drive placeholder (OneDrive Files-On-Demand) isn't hydrated. A still-present file then looked absent → locallyPresent=false DEFEATED the existing C1 read-failure guard (which requires locallyPresent) → decide()=delete-remote → an UNGUARDED tombstone (delete-remote had no absence/bulk guard), which on the next restart delete-locals fleet-wide. This is the SelfSync-side latent cause of the 'all plugins vanished from the list after restart' CLASS. NOTE: it did NOT cause the specific field report — that vault's server index had 0 tombstones (proving SelfSync deleted nothing there; its config sync was pointed at an offline local server), and the true cause was OneDrive Files-On-Demand dehydrating the plugin files so Obsidian couldn't read them at startup. But this is exactly the trap OneDrive-style placeholders + config sync ON + a reachable server would spring. FIX: delete-remote now requires CONFIRMED absence via a direct per-path probe (confirmedAbsent — io.exists/read, never the listing); an unreadable-but-existing file is KEPT. enumerateConfig now LOGS a dir-list failure instead of silently treating it as empty. Correct-by-construction, not a bulk guard (per the owner's explicit direction). Regression: reconcile.test 'CONFIRMED absence' (fail-first verified: guard disabled → the placeholder test fails; genuine deletes still propagate). Severity High (data-loss class). discoveredInField=false (found by analysis while diagnosing the OneDrive report).

rows.title: reconcileAll's bulk-delete guard was ASYMMETRIC: mass delete-REMOTE was unguarded, so a vanished LOCAL vault wiped the server fleet-wide
rows.description: CLIENT-1 (HIGH, data loss). The bulk-delete protection (guardBulkDelete via runDeleteGuard + DeleteRateGuard) was computed from wouldDelete = basePaths.filter(!remote.has(p) && local.has(p)) — ONLY delete-LOCAL candidates — and checked ONLY in reconcileOne's delete-local branch. The delete-remote branch had just the per-file confirmedAbsent probe, no bulk guard. confirmedAbsent catches a placeholder/unreadable listing but NOT a genuine mass local loss (cloud de-hydration, a partial backup restore, cleared storage): every file is truly absent, so each becomes an unbounded d.api.deleteFile → the whole server vault is deleted and tombstoned fleet-wide, then delete-local'd on every peer. The DI-1 bulk-delete hardening only covered the mirror (server-lost-files) direction. FIX: compute wouldDeleteRemote (accepted base paths gone locally but present+unchanged on the server, r.hash===base.hash) and gate the delete-remote branch on a symmetric isSuspiciousBulkDelete(basePaths.length, wouldDeleteRemote, false) — ratio + BULK_DELETE_MIN floor, NO empty-local override (an empty local vault can be a legit last-file delete, unlike an empty server manifest). Fail-first tests: a 10-file vault that vanishes is guarded (server intact); a single-file delete still propagates. Severity High. discoveredInField=false (critique pass, pre-release).

rows.title: 1.7.0 frontmatter parser corrupts block-scalar notes (indented --- false-closes) + rewrites BOM/EOL/key-order on stamp
rows.description: Found by the pre-release 3-lens critique and VERIFIED against shipped 1.7.0: the line-based split() closed the block at the FIRST line trimming to '---', so an indented '---' inside a YAML block scalar (description: | ... '  ---') false-closed the frontmatter and DEMOTED real keys (title, tags) into the body — silent, permanent corruption, written to disk and pushed. Separately setManagedValue stripped a leading BOM, converted CRLF->LF, and reordered keys, while the enable-confirm falsely claimed 'won't touch your other frontmatter'. Reachable for any user who ENABLED embedded timestamps (default off, limited exposure) editing a note with a block-scalar-containing-'---'. FIX (1.7.1): col-0-only fence detection (block-scalar-safe) + surgical writes preserving BOM/EOL/key-order/all non-managed content, with block-scalar/BOM/CRLF/order/round-trip tests as the permanent guard. Severity High (silent data corruption in shipped code). discoveredInField=false (critique-found, before field amplification).

rows.title: A hard auth failure (rejected sign-in / 401) is retried forever like a network drop — hammering login into a server-side lockout, and mislabeled 'offline'
rows.description: Owner-reported with a device log: after a token rejection at reconnect, the client looped 'connect FAILED: unauthorized' every ~15-30s for 45+ min, never prompting re-auth. Root cause: SyncEngine.failToOffline collapsed EVERY effect failure into ONE 'offline' state + ONE recovery (scheduleReconnect, backoff capped 30s), and doConnect's catch distinguished only 404/session-expired via lastIssue string REGEXES; a 401-login or a 429 fell through to retry-forever. Two compounding harms: (1) the storm can trip the server's own 10-fails/5-min LoginThrottle (throttle.rs) → a self-inflicted 429 lockout that persists (every attempt keeps the window from rolling); (2) isAuthError = /HTTP 401/ never matched the server's plain-text 'unauthorized' body (errText overwrites the HTTP-nnn string), so the reactive re-login-once ALSO never fired for a real status() 401. The status card mislabeled a rejected sign-in / a timeout as 'offline'. FIX (connectionFsmTypedFailure, 1.9.1): a typed-failure connection FSM — a separate LinkState machine + a pure classifier reading TAGGED error fields (never a message regex) + a recovery policy — that STOPS retrying on a terminal class (awaits the user + a slow self-heal re-probe), honors the 429 Retry-After window, and surfaces the specific reason; isAuthError fixed to read the status field. Guard (D0047): the connstate tests (classify table + strand/loop invariants). Severity High (self-inflicted lockout + can't sync + confusing state). discoveredInField=true (owner, real device log).

rows.title: Embedded-timestamp backfill flooded the vault with timestamp-only conflict copies (planBackfillItem needsCopy true for every no-frontmatter note)
rows.description: Owner-reported: 'tons of conflict files that show no difference either... on most of these conflict files the only differences I observe are in the timestamps, which we were explicitly supposed to ignore.' Root cause: planBackfillItem computed needsCopy = normalizedContent(original) !== normalizedContent(conformed); for a note with NO frontmatter, conform ADDS a ---...--- block, so the two normalized strings always differ -> needsCopy=true -> a reversible conflict copy for essentially every plain note. On the real vault this produced 33 live conflict copies (32 timestamp/EOL-only + 1 real). FIX (timestampIgnoreRedesign, 1.9.0): the whole backfill (and its needsCopy path) is DELETED — SelfSync never conforms/writes, so no copies are spawned; a timestamp-only cross-device diff is resolved by identity masking with no copy. The 32 existing spurious copies were cleaned up (delete-only, reversible external backup). Severity High (mass spurious conflict copies obscuring real ones). discoveredInField=true.

rows.title: Embedded-timestamp backfill FABRICATED created dates — a copied vault's ctime=copy-time was seeded as created:now
rows.description: Owner-reported on the real vault C:\ otes\\ASI - Work: 'how is it making new files that are created now, when they clearly weren't (their original creation date isn't being respected).' Root cause: the 1.8.0 backfill seeded a missing created from OS metadata (ctime/mtime); the vault is a COPY, and Windows resets file-creation time to copy-time, so seedValues read ctime≈now and stamped created:<today>. detectRestoreSignature (a 5s bucket) was too narrow to notice a slow multi-file copy and suppress the seed. ~22 survivors ended at a fabricated created:2026-07-08 (an earlier Win32 backfill) + others at today; one note has created AFTER updated (provably fabricated). FIX (timestampIgnoreRedesign, 1.9.0): SelfSync writes NO timestamps at all, so it can never fabricate one. Existing fabricated dates are irrecoverable for a real subset (no git; copy-contaminated birth time) and are REPORTED, never invented (the cleanup is delete-only). Severity High (silent wrong data written into user notes). discoveredInField=true.

rows.title: A vault change via the setup wizard skips the merge/direction transition and reconciles against a STALE base — silent overwrite risk (data-integrity)
rows.description: Owner-reported after a reconnect: 'i reconnected but didn't get the modal i expected (merge / keep device's / synced's)... joining a new vault needs some kind of transition logic, unless the re-logging in really did intelligently decide it wasn't needed.' Investigation (verified): a plain reconnect to the SAME vault correctly skips the modal (base intact -> normal incremental resume — WORKING AS DESIGNED, the modal is not broken). BUT a real latent GAP: SetupWizardModal.finish() (setupwizard.ts:255-279) writes st.vaultId directly WITHOUT setting pendingSwitch, WITHOUT clearing the base, and WITHOUT any direction modal, then reconnect() -> doConnect runs reconcileFull over the OLD vault's base. The base is a single global store cleared only by switchTo (reconcile.ts:1167). So changing vaults through the wizard (manually picking another vault, or the previously-synced vault no longer existing -> fallback to vaults[0]) makes decide() run against a FOREIGN base; the B===L->pull branch then SILENTLY OVERWRITES a local file whose new-vault copy differs — no conflict-copy, no prompt. Reachable from the user's exact scenario (token idle-expiry -> freshLogin -> openSetup -> wizard). FIX (vaultChangeTransitionGuard): route a wizard vault-change through switchToVault; defense-in-depth tag the base with owner/vaultId and force a switch/clear when it mismatches. Severity High (silent data overwrite on a vault change). discoveredInField=true.

rows.title: Hot-load privacy gate (1.11.0) rides a STALE vaultIsPrivate — RCE-barrier bypass: a private->shared switch or an out-of-band grant lets a peer's synced main.js auto-execute with no restart
rows.description: Security critic finding, verified in code: vaultIsPrivate is never reset on a vault switch; flushConfigReload (which hot-loads) runs BEFORE the connect-time refreshVaultPrivacy (itself fire-and-forget void); and the delta/poll path that also hot-loads never refreshes it. So switching from a private vault to a shared/attacker vault, OR receiving an out-of-band readWrite grant on your own vault, leaves the gate true -> applyPluginCodeChange hot-loads a peer-controlled plugin (loadManifests+enablePlugin) with no restart — a bypass of the R14 sec#1 never-auto-execute barrier, within the in-scope peer/shared-vault threat model. FIX (hotLoadPrivacyGateFreshCheck, 1.11.1): re-derive privacy FRESH at the decision point. discoveredInField=false (critique-found).

rows.title: A routine mid-session token expiry on the poll/reconcile path mis-classifies as a PERMANENT auth block ('check your password') — the inverse of the auth-storm the FSM fixed
Vault-identity key is SERVER-BLIND (owner/vault) — repointing at a different server with the same vault name silently overwrites local files (D0047 guard never trips)
During a failing/empty initial connect reconcile the card reads 'Synced (polling)' — markReconciling pre-flips to 'syncing', which effectivePhase collapses to idle when 0 files transfer
rows.description: After switchAbortOnOutage (1.11.4) the switch correctly aborted on the DNS outage (connect FAILED -> retrying in 3s), but the owner's log/UI still showed 'Synced (polling)' during the failing ~30s connect attempts — 'nothing to indicate work is being done'. Root cause (one FSM layer below the pure-projection fix): markReconciling() optimistically flipped connecting/disconnected -> reconciling (phase 'syncing') the instant the health check passed, before the initial reconcile ran; when that reconcile transferred nothing (DNS failing), syncPending stayed 0 and effectivePhase collapsed syncing-0-pending -> idle -> a FALSE 'Synced (polling)'. A normal poll avoided this by never pre-flipping (beginReconcile escalates only on real work). FIX (connectPhaseNoOptimisticFlip, 1.11.5): removed markReconciling; beginReconcile is the single door into 'reconciling', escalating from idle OR an in-flight connect, and onProgress(pending>0) triggers it — so a failing/empty connect stays 'Connecting…'/'Reconnecting…'. discoveredInField=true (owner, mobile).

rows.title: DELETE has no optimistic-concurrency (CAS) guard, unlike COMMIT — a stale reconcile delete silently supersedes a newer concurrent commit (L-1 lost update)
rows.description: STPA-UCA hunt finding (server delete control action, L-1). Vault::commit CAS-guards optimistic concurrency (expected_version: a second committer based on a stale version 409s + re-reconciles + merges), with a code comment naming the lost-update it prevents. Vault::delete had NO such guard: it took only a path and computed new_version unconditionally. So a device holding a STALE base could delete a file another device just edited (A commits edit v5->v6; B, still at v5, deletes -> server tombstones at v7), and the editor pulls the tombstone and silently loses its change FLEET-WIDE with no conflict marker — the exact class commit's CAS exists to stop. Weaponizable: a readWrite grantee can DELETE to discard the owner's concurrent edit. The critic flagged it as a possible 'delete-authoritative' trade-off that was NOWHERE recorded as a Decision, with the CAS rationale arguing against it — 'warrants an explicit decision.' OWNER DECISION (AskUserQuestion, 2026-08-02): CAS-guard delete (symmetric with commit) over accept-authoritative. FIX (deleteRemoteCasGuard): Vault::delete_checked(path, expected_version) mirrors commit's CAS (AlreadyExists->409); the reconcile delete-remote sends the based-on remote version; deliberate/authoritative deletes (user gesture / adjudication / switch) omit it and still always win. On a 409 the client re-reconciles and, because decide() keys on hashes, remote-advanced-since-base reads as edit-wins-pull -> the edit is RESURRECTED, never lost. Backward-compatible both ways (old client omits the field; old server ignores the unknown query param). discoveredInField=false (STPA-hunt-found).

rows.title: On mobile, a connection that failed while backgrounded does not re-attempt on resume — the backoff timer is suspended and onResume's remote event is dropped while disconnected
rows.description: Owner (mobile), server URL confirmed reachable: the plugin appeared to stop rechecking after a failed connect — 'is it rechecking though? I don't see it reattempt.' Root cause (mobile context-switching): the backoff reconnect timer uses window.setTimeout, which the OS SUSPENDS while the app is backgrounded, so a pending retry sits paused; and onResume enqueued a `remote` event, which the engine DROPS while disconnected (work is ignored until connected). So foregrounding after a failed connect did nothing to re-attempt. FIX (resumeReattemptsConnection, 1.11.7): onResume, when disconnected, cancels the stale paused timer and enqueues a fresh `connect` immediately (+ logs 'app resumed — re-checking the connection' for visibility); connected → re-assess; 'off' left alone. discoveredInField=true (owner, mobile).

rows.title: Status card latches 'Switching vault… applying your choice' on a persisted pendingSwitch even while connected + synced (no switch initiated); an authoritative switch that lingered set also re-clobbers local edits every connect
rows.description: Owner-reported on a real device: the mobile status card showed 'Switching vault… applying your choice' persistently while the vault was actually connected and synced (green dot, recent Last synced), with no switch initiated. Root cause: statusDisplay() short-circuited on settings.pendingSwitch (a PERSISTED config value = the switch resolution) and this.resuming (a loose bool) BEFORE consulting the pure Phase projection — so a pendingSwitch that lingered set (its switchTo reconcile killed mid-flight on mobile before it could clear) latched the label. The D0047 guard was confirmed NOT the trigger (no 'base belonged to' line in the owner's debug log). Second-order (critique HIGH): a lingering AUTHORITATIVE resolution (download=take-remote / upload=take-local) re-runs on every connect and re-clobbers local edits made since. FIX (statusDisplayPureProjection, 1.11.3): statusDisplay is a PURE Phase projection (no setting/flag read); an already-applied guard clears a lingering switch whose base already belongs to the target (no re-clobber); the settings-card dot is made realtime-aware (no divergence). discoveredInField=true (owner, mobile).

rows.title: A vault switch (upload/download) swallows a whole-server outage (DNS unresolvable) as per-file skips and settles to a FALSE 'Synced (polling)' — the status lies when the server is unreachable
rows.description: Owner's 1.11.3 debug log on mobile: a persisted 'upload' switch ran during a DNS outage (Unable to resolve host 'notes2.willweatherholtz.com') and produced a flood of per-file 'UnknownHostException … skipped it, other files continue', after which the status card showed 'Synced (polling)' (yellow) even though the server was completely unreachable. Root cause: the normal reconcile loops (reconcileAll/reconcileLocalConfig) abort a pass on isConnectionError (→ engine offline+backoff), but switchTo's helpers switchDownload/switchUpload did NOT — every server-op catch called onFileError (skip+continue). So a connection-wide outage was isolated per-file, the switch 'completed' with everything skipped, and the engine settled to idle → a false 'synced'. FIX (switchAbortOnOutage, 1.11.4): switchDownload (applyPull) + switchUpload (pushFile, deleteFile) re-throw on isConnectionError, mirroring reconcileAll → the switch aborts → 'Reconnecting…' (honest). The underlying host-unresolvable condition is the owner's network/server to diagnose. discoveredInField=true (owner, mobile).

rows.title: An upload vault-switch tombstones a remote file that io.list() transiently FALSELY omits — fleet-wide delete-local of a still-present file (L-1)
rows.description: STPA-UCA hunt finding (delete-remote guideword): switchUpload's remote-drop loop issued delete-remote — a server tombstone that propagates delete-local to every peer — for any path missing from the switch's SINGLE io.list() snapshot, with NO probePresence re-probe and NO bulk-ratio guard. io.list() is fallible (an un-hydrated OneDrive/cloud placeholder, a directory that fails to enumerate, an OS/AV lock transiently under-reports a still-present file — the exact issueFalseAbsenceDelete hazard). On an 'upload' switch (make this vault authoritative) such a file is then never pushed AND deleteFile'd on the server; peers see the tombstone and remove their genuine local copy (L-1 data loss), while this device keeps the bytes with no base entry until the next full scan. This was the ONE delete path that trusted the raw listing: reconcileOne + reconcileDelta re-probe via probePresence and switchDownload's local-mirror carries the bulk-ratio guard — switchUpload had neither. FIX (switchUploadProbeGuard, 1.11.8): re-probe (probePresence) before tombstoning; present/indeterminate ⇒ keep. Severity High (fleet-wide delete of real content; recovery timing/luck-dependent via .trash + next full scan). discoveredInField=false (STPA-hunt-found).

rows.title: Composed-vaults mount correctness depends on each mount getting its OWN BaseStore + SyncState + cursor — the pure MountedIo/MountedApi adapters cannot enforce it, and a SHARED base would cause a phantom mass-delete
rows.description: Surfaced by the independent security critique of mountIoAdapters (composed-vaults Phase 2, finding C1 HIGH). The MountedIo/MountedApi adapters re-key a mount into mount-relative path space, but reconcileAll's path universe is (local ∪ remote ∪ base.paths()). If the Phase-3 mount engine wiring hands a mount the PRIMARY scope's BaseStore/SyncState (full-vault paths) instead of a fresh mount-scoped one, every primary path would read as local-absent + base-present under the mount's re-keyed io/api → a phantom mass delete-local/delete-remote (the delete-guard may or may not catch it). The pure adapters CANNOT defend this — base/state are injected by the caller — so it is a load-bearing WIRING invariant: the mount engine MUST allocate each mount its own persisted base + cursor + subscription, verified in the wiring increment's tests. Marked by a load-bearing invariant comment at the head of mountio.ts. discoveredInField=false (critique-found). Severity High (silent bulk data loss if the wiring gets it wrong — a design hazard for the not-yet-built engine, not a defect in shipped behavior). Resolver: the mountEngine action (Phase 3), which allocates + tests per-mount base/state isolation.

rows.title: Deleting the local mount-point FOLDER on a sync mount propagates as a full source-subtree delete — a container deletion must not wipe the (shared) source
rows.description: Owner-raised after D0043. With the mountSyncPushLocal push-back + D0043 (outgoing deletes exact), deleting the whole local mount-point folder fires a delete per child -> nudge -> forceFull -> delete-remote each -> the entire mounted subtree is deleted from the (possibly shared) SOURCE vault server-side. A container deletion reads as remove/reset-the-mount, NOT delete-all-these-shared-files-forever, so it must never wipe the source. OWNER DECISION (flag-and-choose; 'it was intentionally deleted, it should be intentionally reinstantiated'): detect the mount-point folder is gone while the mount had content (base non-empty) -> do NOT reconcile/propagate (critical safety) -> FLAG the mount (surfaced on status + settings) with explicit actions Reinstate (drop base + re-create folder + full re-pull from source) and Remove mount (detach, source preserved) — NO automatic action. Distinguish from a fresh never-materialized mount (base empty -> normal pull). discoveredInField=true (owner). Severity High (a routine folder deletion silently wipes a shared source subtree server-side).

rows.title: A read-write (sync) composed mount does not push LOCAL edits back to the source in steady state — the mount poll is source-driven only
rows.description: Owner field report, CONFIRMED by trace. pollMount (mountsync.ts:30-44) calls changes() on the SOURCE, then runs reconcileDelta (applies the source delta = pull) when the source changed, or noop+returns when it did not; only a FORCED FULL pass (reconcileAll, on first-mount/reconnect/Keep) scans LOCAL files. So a local create/edit/delete in a sync-mount folder whose source is unchanged is never scanned or pushed to the source — mounts react to source changes, never to local changes (unlike the primary, which is driven by local file events). Effect: a sync mount is one-directional in practice (pulls from source, never pushes local edits back) until a reconnect forces a full pass. NOT data loss (the local file is safe on disk) but the sync contract is broken. FIX: route a local file event under a mount point to a full (local-scanning) reconcile for that mount. discoveredInField=true (owner). Severity High (a sync mount silently fails to propagate the user's local edits to the shared source).

rows.title: Redeeming a share link for a vault YOU OWN stamps vaultOwner with your own name → connect-time grant check reports 'revoked' and blocks ALL sync
The wire-compat gate treats an OPTIONAL response field the client added (that an older server lacks) as BREAKING — a newer client hard-blocks sync against an older / mid-redeploy server
rows.description: OWNER FIELD REPORT (2026-08-15): after updating BOTH server and client to 1.29.0, the client refused to sync — 'the server dropped Deletion.author/device_id/device_name, which this plugin reads. Update whichever is older.' Those are the OPTIONAL provenance fields the 1.29 client itself added (read undefined-safe). ROOT CAUSE: diffSignature's RESPONSE branch flagged ANY field in the client's embedded signature that the server lacks as breaking, REGARDLESS of `required`. So a NEWER client (which added optional response fields) hard-blocks sync against an OLDER server — or, transiently, a server MID-REDEPLOY (the log showed a block at 12:37 then a clean sync at 12:38 once the new image was live). This BROKE backward compatibility (a 1.29 client cannot sync with any pre-1.29 server) and made the deletion-provenance rollout require a lock-step update. Secondary: the message 'Update whichever is older' never says WHICH side. FIX (client-only): an optional (required:false) response field the server lacks is NON-breaking (the client degrades to undefined) — only a REQUIRED one gates; a guard test allowlists every optional response field as undefined-safe so a future one forces review; and a directional hint tells the user which side is likely older (server-lacks → server, hedged for the just-updated case; server-demands → plugin). discoveredInField=true. Severity High (blocks ALL sync against an older/mid-redeploy server; a backward-compat regression from 1.29.0).

rows.title: Case-only folder capitalisation difference between a Windows vault and the server made every file in those folders unpushable - and edits there silently did not sync
rows.description: Confirmed 2026-09-07 from the owner's 1.30.9 log: every refused push read 'the server refused it - a path differing only in case already exists' - hundreds of files under 4 Archive/**, 3 Resources/**, 2 Areas/**, 99 Utilities/**. The server's index holds those folders in a different capitalisation than this Windows vault reports. Path identity in the client was exact-case everywhere (base keys, manifest keys, decide()), while the filesystem underneath is case-insensitive, so a case-only divergence produced: (a) the local spelling has no base/remote key -> decide() = local-only-new -> push -> the server's collision guard refuses it (correctly - it protects case-sensitive servers from two keys folding onto one file); (b) the server's spelling is 'absent' from the local listing, but the false-absence re-probe (adapter.exists, case-insensitive) says present -> no delete -> the pair never converges; (c) and the DATA hazard: an edit made under the local spelling changes a file the client can only push under a refused key - edits in those folders did not sync at all, silently, since whenever the capitalisation diverged. Performance was the visible symptom (~500 futile uploads per pass, 1.30.9 held them after the first pass); the silent non-sync of edits is the real defect. FIX (casePathAlias): on case-insensitive platforms the local spelling is aliased to the existing server/base key for sync identity, in the full pass, the config pass and the vault-event path; nothing is renamed; the server keeps its spelling; Linux/Android untouched. ROOT CAUSE of the divergence itself (which device re-capitalised the folders, and when) is not knowable from the record; the client must simply be correct under it. discoveredInField = true. Severity High: silent non-sync of edits in a whole folder tree.

rows.title: Server-refused pushes (commit: HTTP 400) were re-sent on every pass with the reason thrown away - ~500 futile uploads per reconcile made the UI crawl
rows.description: Owner field report 2026-09-07: 'it's much slower now' - opening the Resolve-conflicts modal, clicking anything. The debug log showed why: the connect pass was PUSHING several hundred files under the PARA roots (4 Archive/**, 3 Resources/**, 2 Areas/**, 99 Utilities/**) - notes, PDFs, images alike - and the server answered 'commit: HTTP 400' for every one; 'checked 750/1835 files' arrived at +118.8s and the pass was still running at +165s, on a vault whose no-op rescan the perf harness completes in ~150 ms. Two client defects made this what it was. (1) transport.commit threw a bare 'commit: HTTP 400', discarding the server's body - which is the client-actionable reason (the server returns validation failures verbatim) - so neither the user nor the code could see WHY. (2) reconcile treated a 400 like any transient per-file error: the next pass re-read, re-chunked, queried missing chunks, re-uploaded and re-committed the identical content, and was refused again - for every file, every pass, forever. The reconcile loop runs on the renderer's main thread with the modal and settings tab, hence 'clicking anything' is slow. FIX (rejectedPushHold): a typed CommitRejectedError carrying the server text; a (path -> refused hash) memo so an unchanged rejected file is HELD (one summary log line per burst) until it is edited or the plugin reloads; 409/404 stay retryable. ROOT CAUSE OF THE REFUSALS IS STILL OPEN and will be named by 1.30.9's log. Leading hypothesis from the evidence: every rejected path sits under a top-level folder whose CAPITALISATION may differ between this Windows vault and the server's index keys - the server's commit guard refuses 'a path differing only in case already exists' - i.e. a case-only folder rename on a case-insensitive filesystem, which decide() sees as a local-only-new file (push) plus a remote file that a presence re-probe says is still present (no delete), so the two never converge. If confirmed, the fix is case-aware path identity on case-insensitive filesystems (a follow-up issue with its own resolver). discoveredInField = true. Severity High: the sync loop was doing hundreds of futile uploads per pass and the UI was unusable while it ran.

rows.title: 'That file changed since you opened this' fired when nothing had changed - a read failure and any cosmetic rewrite both counted as a change, blocking the apply
rows.description: Owner field report: 'claims things have changed since i last opened the file which i haven't done'. The stale-preview guard in resolveNoteConflict compared (await readTextOrEmpty(original)) !== previewedOther. TWO independent false positives. (a) readTextOrEmpty SWALLOWS every read error and returns the empty string, so a transient Windows lock / AV scan / cloud placeholder read as 'the file was rewritten' - the user is told someone else edited their note when the file merely could not be opened for a moment. (b) The comparison was on RAW decoded text while the modal's own diff NORMALIZES EOL and (now) masks ignored timestamp keys - so a CRLF rewrite, or a `modified:`/`updated:` bump by another plugin, or an engine re-write during the 4s safety-net poll while the modal sat open, refused the apply over a difference the user was never shown. Because it is the 'Keep this device's' path that is guarded, the effect is that the user cannot keep their own version. FIXED by previewStillCurrent returning match/changed/unreadable and judging on normalizedContent - the same content identity the sync engine uses - with a distinct 'couldn't read it' notice. A genuine body change still refuses (guarded). discoveredInField=true.

rows.title: Resolve-conflicts modal hung indefinitely on a ~200 MB .mp4 conflict - it read both versions as text and line-diffed them
rows.description: Owner field report 2026-09-08: 'resolve totally hangs - i see no diff, just 2 files need review. Looks like it's an mp4 that multiple files edited at once (which almost surely didn't actually happen)'. The vault holds a conflict copy of a ~200 MB .mp4 (the same recording the size gate logs as 'over this device's 200 MB sync limit'). NoteConflictModal.render read BOTH versions with readTextOrEmpty - TextDecoder over 200 MB on the renderer's main thread, twice - then handed the two giant strings to unifiedLineDiff and revealInvisible: a multi-second-to-indefinite freeze with nothing on screen but the header, i.e. 'totally hangs'. The 1.30.5 cosmetic-conflict sweep already gated on isTextExt/strictDecode; the modal's own render path never did, so the one surface a user reaches for on a binary conflict was the one that could not survive it. FIX (conflictModalBinaryView): decide from fileStat (no read) - binary extension or text > 4 MB -> the no-diff view (sizes + dates per side, same keep choices, nothing read, no stale-preview guard because nothing was previewed). WHY THE MP4 HAD A CONFLICT COPY AT ALL (not fixed here, likely benign): the file is the meeting recording that was still being written into the vault while a pull ran, and conflictCopyIfRaced preserves a local file whose bytes changed during a pull as a copy - or the recording crossed the 200 MB limit between devices; either produces exactly one copy and no data loss. discoveredInField = true. Severity High: the resolve surface hung indefinitely on a real conflict.

rows.title: A case-only rename made on a case-sensitive peer deletes the note fleet-wide on folding peers
rows.description: Panel 2026-09-11 (host critic, H1 BLOCKER + H2..H7): tombstone `Note.md` + upsert `note.md` in one pass name ONE on-disk file on Windows/macOS/iOS; removeLocal deleted the file the upsert adopted and the host's delete event then tombstoned the new key for every peer (H-1, H-11; SR-45 unmet). Also: an in-flight pass keeps writing after onunload (SR-44's safe state false); the mobile per-file cap equals the desktop default (OOM path); persist() runs on every setBase (a whole-data.json write loop); short writes in the streamed writer; the fold index rebuilt per event; timers not cleared on unload. Resolver: sprint hostCoexistenceHardening.

rows.title: A release is BRAT-installable before it is verified, a tag can be silently reused, integrity has no anchor outside the release, and no version-tagged server image exists
rows.description: Panel 2026-09-11 (release-channel critic, RL1..RL6): release.yml published non-draft before the verify step and treated a partial upload as released; `gh release create --target` reuses a tag pointing elsewhere (assets = build of main-HEAD); SHA256SUMS lives in the same mutable release as the assets, so the daily check could not detect a rewrite of both (H-5); GITHUB_TOKEN-created tags never trigger server-image.yml, so the version-tagged image docs tell operators to pin never existed; mutable action refs, persisted checkout credentials, no Dependabot; check-release.mjs hid gh's real error and downloaded every asset. Resolver: sprint releaseIntegrityHardening (D0054 amended).

rows.title: Three accepted Decisions' text drifted after acceptance; keel 0.4.1's acceptance-binds-to-text guard blocks every commit until the owner re-binds
rows.description: keel 0.4.1 (D0308, HARD): d0014, d0025, d0046 - their decision/consequences text at HEAD differs from the text at the SHA their acceptance bound to (editorial edits by the agent on 2026-07-05, 2026-07-12, 2026-09-07). The only remedy is the human's `keel accept <d> --rebind --note ...`. Surfaced by the D0057 resync; owner-only.

rows.title: Seven compound Decisions (created on/after 2026-09-05) violate D0303 option C; keel 0.4.1's decision-scaffolding guard blocks every commit until split or grandfathered
rows.description: keel 0.4.1 (D0303 option C, HARD): d0046, d0048, d0050, d0051, d0053, d0054, d0055 enumerate 2-8 clauses each; the guard wants one Decision per clause with #DependsOn edges. Four are already accepted, so a split re-proposes them (about thirty owner acceptances). Owner policy: split here, or an upstream cutoff/grandfather. Surfaced by the D0057 resync.

rows.title: Deleting an account leaves its vault data on disk; reusing the username inherits it
rows.description: SEC-MED-2: users_delete removes the record + shares + tokens but never removes DATA_ROOT/<name>/, so recreating the name silently adopts the prior owner's notes. Fix: remove/quarantine the data dir on delete (or refuse to reuse a name with residual data).

rows.title: A throw from the status-callback dispatch (set before the try) leaked the `applying` lock true forever
Unauthenticated argon2 flood on /api/login ran on async workers with no length cap or concurrency bound
rows.description: SEC#2: login ran the memory-hard argon2 verify directly on a tokio worker, holding the users mutex, with no password-length cap — a concurrent flood (optionally multi-MB passwords) exhausts CPU/RAM. Fixed: cap password length (1 KiB), release the lock first, run argon2 on a blocking thread bounded by an 8-permit semaphore; register offloaded too.

rows.title: commit writes the bind-mount file before the durable journal; a crash + reindex resurrects uncommitted content
rows.description: DI-3: std::fs::write precedes the journal append; a crash/rollback in that window leaves disk ahead of the index, and reindex (which rebuilds from disk) then makes the never-committed body canonical. Fix: write the file after the journal is durable (temp + rename post-journal).

rows.title: Config edit-vs-delete silently resurrected a removed config file / reverted a removal
rows.description: CO-3: config edit-wins-* fell through instead of adjudicating, contradicting the never-resurrect invariant (edit-wins-pull pulled a locally-deleted config back). Fixed: config edit-vs-delete is adjudicated like divergence.

rows.title: Merge/conflict copies preserved the stale pre-fetch local read, not a racing edit
rows.description: DI-R2#5: the merge/conflict-copy and read-only-share fallbacks wrote the localBytes read before the remote fetch as the conflict copy, so an edit made DURING the fetch was lost. Fixed: re-read current on-disk bytes for the copy. Also: bulk-delete ratio denominator now counts only accepted base paths (note).

rows.title: A directly-attempted local op that failed was neither re-queued nor retried
rows.description: CONC-R2#2: onLocalEvent/Delete/Rename only logged on catch, relying on the next full reconcile; on an idle remote a transient failure left the edit unsynced for a long time. Fixed: re-queue the path(s) into pendingLocal on catch so the drain retries.

rows.title: The per-file event path applied only the empty-manifest delete guard, not the widened ratio guard
rows.description: DI#5: reconcilePath set guardDelete only when the whole manifest was empty, so a PARTIAL server index loss slipped delete-local through the event path (which handles most live-editing deletions). Fixed: reconcilePath computes the same base-missing ratio guard reconcileAll uses.

rows.title: No rate-limiting on /api/login (+ open /api/register); each attempt runs argon2
rows.description: SEC-MED-3: unauthenticated auth endpoints run a full argon2 verify/hash per request with no throttle, enabling online brute force + CPU/RAM-exhaustion DoS. Fix: per-IP + per-account rate limiting/backoff + a concurrency cap.

rows.title: pushBytes discarded committed bytes; clean-merge base could record disagreeing (text,hash)
rows.description: DI-R2#3: the merge path set base from pre-write merged bytes while the hash came from pushFile's re-read — a racing save between them desynced base.text vs base.hash, poisoning the next merge's ancestor. Fixed: pushBytes returns PushResult; base recorded from committed bytes (DI-5 on the merge path).

rows.title: Non-canonical path (notes//a.md, trailing slash) desyncs the raw index key from the on-disk name
rows.description: DI-R4#1 (MED): commit used the RAW req.path as the index key but derived the on-disk mirror from a Path-normalized value that collapses redundant/trailing slashes, so a non-conforming/hostile client could commit two keys (notes/a.md + notes//a.md) aliasing ONE disk file (silent overwrite + double manifest entry → client phantom-delete ping-pong), or desync key-vs-disk (reindex brick). Same integrity boundary as the case-collision/junk/trailing-dot guards. Fixed: safe_rel_path rejects any path that isn't its own canonical forward-slash form. +test.

rows.title: The imperative main.ts orchestration layer (incl. 2 MUST reqs + the SEC-3 gate + WS push) has no automated tests
rows.description: Holistic#2/#3/#4 (MED, OPEN): srConfigLiveDetect + srSelfHealingReconnect (both priority=must), the SEC-3 no-plugin-code-from-shared-vault gate, and WS instant-push + revocation eviction are verified by inspect+attestation only — reconnect/scheduleReconnect/connectWs/onRawConfigEvent/flushRawConfig/flushConfigReload have zero test references. This is the 0.10.4-escape code family; a regression wouldn't fail CI. Extract the FSM + raw-event pipeline into injectable units (like the pure modules) and test them. Pre-broad-release.

rows.title: Uncommitted orphan chunks are reclaimed only at startup; no runtime per-vault byte quota
rows.description: SEC#4 (DEFERRED): a ReadWrite grantee (or owner) can PUT unlimited unique chunks that never commit, filling the owner's disk until a restart's GC. Mitigated for now by the lowered 512 MiB per-file ceiling; a per-vault stored-bytes quota / runtime orphan GC is the real fix — deferred as its own change. Authenticated-only, DoS not data-loss.

rows.title: DI-3 racing-edit guard missed the streamed branch and the racing-create case
rows.description: DI-R2#2/#4: applyPull's guard ran only on the buffered path and only when the local file was present, so a large-file stream (or a racing local CREATE of an expected-absent path) silently clobbered local content. Fixed: shared conflictCopyIfRaced + guardRace flag covering both paths and the absent-expected case.

rows.title: A local save landing during a pull's network fetch was silently clobbered (no conflict copy)
rows.description: DI#3: the applying guard serializes reconcile but not the editor's autosave; a save during fetchVerified's multi-chunk fetch was overwritten by the pull and resolved as clean in-sync. Fixed: applyPull re-checks disk just before writing and preserves a changed local file as a conflict copy.

rows.title: Username enumeration via /api/register (409 exists vs 403 closed) before the invite gate
rows.description: SEC-MED-1: the exists() check returns 409 before the closed-mode/invite 403, so an unauthenticated caller harvests the account list on a closed server. Fix: enforce the invite/mode gate before the existence check; uniform error.

rows.title: reindex over an incomplete vault dir drops absent files from the manifest and GCs their chunks
rows.description: DI-4: reindex rebuilds solely from present files and GCs unreferenced blobs, so a transiently-incomplete dir (partial restore / in-flight copy) becomes permanent loss — feeding DI-1's client deletions. Fix: refuse/preserve when a previously-indexed path is missing from disk during a repair; never GC blobs for prior-index paths.

rows.title: A committed junk-named file (.DS_Store/.git) permanently bricks reindex (cross-account)
rows.description: SEC-R2#2: commit accepted names that reindex's collect_files skips as junk, so a later reindex counted them as 'indexed file missing from disk' (DI-4) and aborted every time — leaving the vault stuck in ERROR; a readWrite grantee could inflict it on the owner. Fixed: safe_rel_path rejects junk basenames. +test.

rows.title: Case-sensitive self-folder exclusion let a shared vault overwrite the victim's SelfSync credentials
rows.description: SEC-R2#1 (MED, connection hijack): shouldSync compared the self-folder path case-sensitively while SEC#1 canonicalized only user/vault segments (not in-vault file paths), so a shared-vault owner committing .obsidian/plugins/NEW-LIVESYNC/data.json overwrote the victim's stored server URL+creds on a case-insensitive FS. Fixed: case-insensitive self-folder exclusion. +test.

rows.title: Trailing-dot/space names bypassed safe_rel_path, desyncing index key vs on-disk name (Windows)
rows.description: SEC-R3#1 (MED): safe_rel_path didn't reject a component ending in '.' or space (or all-dots), which Windows strips on write — so index key 'evil.md.' != on-disk 'evil.md', re-opening the DI-4 reindex-brick, and 'aux ' evaded the reserved-device check (→ AUX). Fixed: reject trailing-dot/space + all-dot components (safe superset on Linux). +test.

rows.title: PROTO-4 case-collision guard folded ASCII only; a Unicode case pair (café/CAFÉ) evaded it
rows.description: DI-R5#1 (LOW-MED, deployment-conditional): eq_ignore_ascii_case let café.md and CAFÉ.md both enter the index while a case-insensitive Unicode-folding FS (macOS/Windows) collapses them to one file → reindex brick + phantom-delete; a readWrite grantee could inflict it. Fixed: fold full Unicode case (to_lowercase) in the collision check. +test.

rows.title: No per-account vault cap: unbounded never-evicted handles + inodes
rows.description: SEC#3: create_vault had no limit; an authenticated user could loop-create unique vaults, each a never-evicted cached handle + directory tree, degrading every tenant (RAM + inodes). Fixed: cap at 100 vaults per account.

rows.title: No client<->server protocol/schema version negotiation (independent-upgrade skew is undiagnosable)
rows.description: Holistic#1 (MED, OPEN): /health returns bare 'ok'; no apiVersion field, no min-client check, and the on-disk Index has no schema tag. The plugin auto-updates (BRAT) independently of the server, so version skew is the most likely real-world breakage — and it surfaces as a generic 'malformed response' retry loop (SAFE, never mutates, but undiagnosable) or a scary CORRUPT→reindex. Add a version handshake + a clear 'incompatible, upgrade' message. Pre-broad-release.

rows.title: Math.max version cursor pinned high after a server rewind, forcing a full reconcile every poll
rows.description: CONC-R2#3: reconcileAll/switchTo advanced the cursor with Math.max, so after a server reindex/restore rewound the version, every idle poll saw a mismatch and re-ran a full reconcile forever. Fixed: ASSIGN resp.version after a full reconcile (the client is consistent with it), so the incremental path converges.

rows.title: A WS-only drop while polling stayed healthy never re-established instant sync
rows.description: CONC#3: connectWs ran only inside reconnect(), which is re-entered only on a POLL failure; a proxy/idle-timeout WS close (with polls still 200) silently degraded the session to 4s polling. Fixed: spinUpWs self-heals via a guarded, delayed re-dial on close, independent of poll health.

rows.title: RS-4: client base keeps the full TEXT of every mergeable file, re-serialized to data.json on every base change
Synced theme/snippet CSS is auto-applied with no trust gate (injection via un-CSP'd renderer)
rows.description: SEC-R6#2 (MED): unlike the plugin branch, the appearance/theme/snippet CSS branch of flushConfigReload had NO ownership guard at all — it unconditionally called customCss.loadData/loadSnippets for any vault. A peer/owner commits malicious CSS; Obsidian's un-CSP'd renderer allows url()/attribute-selector exfil + phishing overlays. Fixed 0.10.27: synced CSS is never auto-applied; the user reloads to apply.

rows.title: failToOffline leaves connected=true -> a WS redial + the backoff reconnect both run (two recovery paths)
RS-3: reconcileAll re-pulls the whole manifest AND re-hashes the whole local vault on ANY remote change
rows.description: RS-R7#3 (scale, mobile even at modest size): doReconcileAll fetches the incremental changes(since) then DISCARDS it and runs reconcileAll (changes(0) + full path-union rehash), so one remote edit re-hashes the entire local vault — seconds-to-minutes of CPU + battery on a large vault on a phone. Storage-independent: reconcile only the delta's paths on a remote poke; full pass only on the periodic config scan / version rewind. Tracked under scaleHardening (first to pull forward).

rows.title: RS-1: VaultHandle map is never evicted — every vault ever opened stays fully resident in RAM
rows.description: RS-R7#1 (scale): the ns map is only inserted-to (removed only on account delete) — no LRU/idle eviction, so a multi-vault server pins every touched vault's whole Index in RAM for process life (~40-60 MB per 100k-file vault). Storage-independent; needs idle-handle eviction. Tracked under scaleHardening.

rows.title: RS-2: every commit/delete deep-clones the ENTIRE index for rollback (O(vault) per write)
rows.description: RS-R7#2 (scale): commit/delete take `self.idx.clone()` (full deep copy of files+deletions+chunk_refs) purely for journal-failure rollback, so per-write cost grows with vault size — large vaults get slower to write regardless of change size. Mooted by the SQLite storage decision (row-level writes, no whole-index clone); until then, a targeted rollback would fix it. Tracked under scaleHardening.

rows.title: RS-5: changes(since) is an O(all files + all tombstones) linear scan run by every device every 4s
rows.description: RS-R7#5 (scale): changes filters both collections by linear scan (no version index); every 4s idle poll from N devices is N x O(files+tombstones) for zero results, and the (now-durable, growing) tombstones make each poll ever more expensive. Mooted by SQLite (indexed WHERE version > ?). Tracked under scaleHardening.

rows.title: Operator toolkit gap: no per-vault delete (only whole-account) and no forced repair
rows.description: RC-R7#4 (MED): the admin surface could create/reindex/share but not delete a single vault (only whole-account users_delete) nor force a repair past an unrecoverable file. Fixed 0.10.28: DELETE /api/admin/vault + admin-UI button (per-vault delete) and the forced reindex (RC-2). Residual (tracked): a UI to reset a latched client-side bulk-delete guard.

rows.title: reindex bypasses the case/Unicode collision + safe_rel_path guards that commit enforces
rows.description: DI-R6#3 (MED): the PROTO-4 case/fold collision guard + safe_rel_path run only on the commit path. reindex (the other way index entries are created) ingested colliding names straight off the Linux bind-mount, minting two index keys that a case-insensitive/Unicode-folding client FS collapses to one file -> overwrite + phantom-delete churn. Fixed 0.10.27: reindex runs the same conflicting_or_unsafe_rels check (unsafe or fold-colliding names abort the reindex with a clear message).

rows.title: Concurrent re-login race clears the password mid-flight (spurious 'session expired' + orphan token)
rows.description: CONC-R6#3 (MED): freshLogin READS the password (loginRemote) then destructively CLEARS it (token-only mode); the engine's reactive-401 path (doConnect) and the non-engine withAuth path (setup/switch modals) can both run it concurrently — a read-modify-write race across await with two entrants. The second reads an emptied password -> spurious 'session expired' prompt while a login is actually succeeding, minting an orphan token. Fixed 0.10.27: freshLogin is single-flight (concurrent calls coalesce into one login).

rows.title: A deleted/missing server vault shows as 'Can't reach the server — retrying' forever
rows.description: RC-R7#3 (MED): doConnect distinguishes 401/version/not-ready but not 404 (vault-not-found), so a deleted/renamed server-side vault collapses into the catch-all connectivity message + indefinite backoff — the server IS reachable, the vault is gone, but the signal says the opposite. Fixed 0.10.28: a 404 surfaces 'this vault no longer exists — re-create or switch (local files untouched)'.

rows.title: Full-manifest changes(since=0) scans SQLite under the read lock on the async worker
rows.description: Conc-R8 M2 (MED): the changes handler holds rlock(vault) and runs SqliteIndex::changes on the async worker; for since=0 (first sync / full reconcile) that's a whole-files-table scan blocking a runtime worker for its duration (the write ops correctly use spawn_blocking; this read path does not). No deadlock (no await under the guard). Fix: offload the full-manifest read to the blocking pool. Lower-impact cousin of the now-fixed cold-open-on-worker (Conc-H1).

rows.title: Concurrent first-access to a cold corrupt vault can leave the cached handle stuck corrupt (SQLITE_BUSY)
rows.description: Conc-R8 M1 (MED): state.vault() releases the ns-map lock across Vault::open, so two concurrent first-accesses to the same cold, corrupt (user,vault) both run reindex on separate SQLite connections. SQLite serializes writers → one hits SQLITE_BUSY, its reindex errors, and that Vault stays corrupt=true; if it wins the or_insert race it's the CACHED handle → every sync op 503s until a manual reindex, though the DB is fine. Fix: a per-(user,vault) open/reindex lock so only one thread opens. Low real-world likelihood (needs simultaneous cold first-access to the same corrupt vault).

rows.title: AU.3.3.1 — failed MFA enable/disable attempts not audited
rows.description: A wrong-code MFA disable (a stolen-token probe to strip the second factor) and a failed enrollment-confirm emitted no audit event — only the success paths did. RESOLVED: mfa.rs emits MFA_DISABLE/MFA_ENABLE with outcome=FAILURE on the wrong-code branches. Class: audit coverage gap.

rows.title: AU.3.3.2/3.3.8 — audit SOURCE spoofable + absent on authz-denied events
rows.description: The audit source takes the leftmost X-Forwarded-For (client-spoofable unless the proxy replaces it), and the cross-tenant/require_admin denial events pass source='-' (IP not threaded into those choke-points). RESOLVED (high-value half): require_admin now threads the caller's ClientIp, so the privileged-function-DENIED events — the assessor's primary concern — carry the source. The lower-value per-vault read denials in scoped() keep source '-' (accepted: proxy-correlated by timestamp), and the XFF-trust remains the documented proxy contract (a spoofed XFF is only possible if the proxy doesn't overwrite it). Class: audit accountability.

rows.title: SC.3.13.8 — client cleartext-http refusal not complete across account calls
rows.description: The 'whole channel' claim was overstated: only the sync constructor + login/register checked isInsecureRemote; the token-bearing account-management static methods (listVaults/createVault/changePassword/shares/myVaults) did not, so a persisted cleartext-remote baseUrl could transmit the token (and a new password) in the clear. RESOLVED: centralized the check in httpReq — every request refuses http-to-remote (loopback still allowed); 3.13.8 now genuinely whole-channel (met). Class: transmission confidentiality (was narrowly overstated).

rows.title: SC.3.13.1 — global WS budget with no per-user sub-cap (single-account notification DoS)
rows.description: MAX_WS_CONNECTIONS was a single global cap, so one authenticated account could open all 512 sockets and deny change-notifications to every other user. RESOLVED: added a per-user WS sub-cap (MAX_WS_PER_USER=16) checked alongside the global reserve, released by the connection guard on every exit path. Class: authenticated availability.

rows.title: 3.13.16: CUI at rest is plaintext (SC)
rows.description: CUI at rest is plaintext (SC.3.13.16). Near-term: operator volume encryption; E2EE deferred.

rows.title: 3.13.11: Crypto is not FIPS-validated (SC)
rows.description: Crypto is not FIPS-validated (SC.3.13.11). Decision: FIPS provider if genuine CUI is stored.

rows.title: 3.5.9: No forced-change-on-reset (IA)
rows.description: No forced-change-on-reset (IA.3.5.9). RESOLVED: admin create/reset flags must_change; the AuthToken extractor blocks every route but change-password/logout until the account sets a new password. Real tests: admin.rs admin_created_account_is_forced_to_change_password_before_use + users.rs must_change_flag_set_clear_and_cleared_on_remove.

rows.title: 3.5.3: No multifactor authentication (IA)
rows.description: No multifactor authentication (IA.3.5.3).
