RESOLVED: TOTP (RFC 6238) second factor + single-use recovery codes for privileged (server-admin) accounts — self-enrolled via /admin, verified at login. Self-contained crypto (totp.rs, no new deps) pinned to RFC 4231/6238 test vectors. Real tests: totp.rs totp_rfc6238_vectors + hmac_sha1_rfc4231; admin.rs mfa_totp_full_lifecycle. Non-privileged (plugin) MFA is a follow-up.

rows.title: 3.5.8: No password-reuse history (IA)
rows.description: No password-reuse history (IA.3.5.8). RESOLVED: users.rs retains the last 5 argon2 hashes and change_password rejects reuse of the current or any recent password. Real tests: users.rs reuse_history_rejects_current_and_recent_passwords + admin.rs password_change_rejects_reuse_of_a_recent_password.

rows.title: 'download' vault-switch bypassed the bulk-delete guard
rows.description: switchTo('download') removed every accepted local file absent from the target manifest with no ratio guard; a target reindexed over a PARTIAL directory reports status:ready while missing files, so mirroring it mass-deleted legitimate local-only notes (recoverable via .trash). RESOLVED: the same BULK_DELETE ratio guard reconcileAll uses now gates the download-mode removal — a suspiciously-incomplete manifest keeps local files (surfaced via onGuard); a genuine populated target still mirrors. Class: recoverable-but-wrong.

rows.title: Mobile buffered write is not fsync-durable (crash-window delete-remote)
rows.description: On mobile io.write can't fsync, so a pulled note's bytes can sit in cache while data.json (the base map) persists; a crash in that window leaves the note absent-on-disk but base==remote, which decide() resolves to delete-remote. ACCEPTED/DEFERRED: inherent to the mobile adapter's lack of an fsync API; desktop is durable. Mitigation options (persist base only after a read-back barrier) tracked. Class: durability (platform-inherent, accepted).

rows.title: delete-local restore push had no CAS → lost update
rows.description: The tombstone-authoritative 'restore, never destroy' branch pushed with no expectedVersion, so a peer that created the path between this device's manifest read and the restore commit was silently overwritten. RESOLVED: the restore commits with expectedVersion 0 ('expected absent') → a concurrent create 409s → next reconcile merges. Class: recoverable-but-wrong.

rows.title: No client-side WebSocket liveness check (half-open socket stalls realtime)
rows.description: The client treated the WS as healthy until the browser fired close; a half-open socket (radio sleep / NAT rebind) kept realtimeConnected true with the poll downshifted, so the light showed green over a dead channel. RESOLVED: the server sends an application heartbeat every ~30s (ws.rs) that the client CAN see (browsers hide protocol ping/pong from JS), and the client runs a liveness timer (isWsStale) that drops realtime health + upshifts the poll + re-dials if no frame arrives within WS_STALE_MS (~75s). Test: syncstate.test isWsStale. Class: latency / misleading state.

rows.title: must_change gate not enforced on the WebSocket path
rows.description: The AuthToken extractor blocks a forced-change account on all HTTP routes, but ws_handler resolved the token manually and skipped the check, so a locked account could still open change-notification subscriptions (metadata only, ACL-gated). RESOLVED: ws_handler now rejects a must_change account with 403, mirroring the extractor. Class: authz gate gap.

rows.title: Plugin P2: config-sync toggles look inert (apply only on the ~2-min tick)
rows.description: Config-sync master/category/plugin toggles only persisted + re-rendered; they took effect only on the next periodic config scan (up to CONFIG_SCAN_INTERVAL_MS ~2 min), so flipping one appeared to do nothing. RESOLVED: applyConfigSyncChange() forces a config scan and kicks a reconcile immediately. Class: switch appears inert.

rows.title: Plugin P4: status light shows green 'Fully synced' while the WebSocket is closed
rows.description: The light was a pure projection of the reconcile FSM phase and never read ws.readyState; on a WS drop with polling still succeeding it stayed green 'Fully synced' though realtime was down. RESOLVED: a realtimeConnected flag threads into light() — idle-without-realtime is no longer green and says it's polling. Class: dual-truth (status vs transport).

rows.title: Admin A2: MFA panel shows 'disabled' after a successful enable
rows.description: MFA confirm succeeded but never re-read status, so the panel kept the enroll/disabled view while the server was enabled. RESOLVED: confirm re-reads status (renderMfa) while preserving the one-time recovery codes. Class: dual-truth/stale indicator.

rows.title: Admin A4: owner-vault sub-row not reconciled after Repair/Delete
rows.description: In the account→Vaults sub-row, Repair/Delete only set a message; the row wasn't re-fetched, so a deleted vault lingered and a repaired vault's health chip stayed stale. RESOLVED: the sub-row re-fetches + re-renders after each action. Class: stale indicator.

rows.title: Admin A5: Repair offered on a 'missing' vault where the endpoint 404s
rows.description: The health chip called a 'missing' vault 'no data yet' but a Repair button was still shown; clicking it 404'd (reindex requires an existing vault). RESOLVED: Repair is gated to genuinely-degraded vaults in both panels. Class: dual-truth (chip vs action).

rows.title: shares.rs grant() leaves an in-memory grant when its save() fails → redeem rollback breaks single-use
rows.description: Concurrency critic (Medium). grant() mutated self.file.grants then save()'d; on a save I/O error (disk full/EIO) the in-memory grant persisted while only Err was returned. The redeem handler, which unredeems (restores the link) on grant Err, then left BOTH a live in-memory grant AND a re-redeemable single-use link — violating single-use and the 'fails closed' contract. RESOLVED (server): grant() snapshots grants, mutates, saves, and restores the snapshot on save failure so in-memory always matches the last durable state. Test: shares grant_rolls_back_in_memory_when_save_fails. Class: cross-store consistency under I/O failure.

rows.title: resolveNoteConflict 'keep mine' TOCTOU — stale-preview guard, then two awaits before the write → a reconcile can be clobbered
rows.description: Concurrency critic (Medium). 'keep mine' checked the stale-preview guard, then yielded twice (io.exists, io.read) before writing original; the modal runs OUTSIDE the engine queue, so a poll-driven reconcile could pull a newer original into that gap and get silently overwritten + pushed. RESOLVED (1.0.31): re-check original===previewedOther immediately before the write (no await between the re-check and the write), narrowing the window to nothing actionable. Class: data-loss (narrow race).

rows.title: Share-link self-redeem (owner redeems own link) burns the single-use invite (contradicts documented no-op)
rows.description: Correctness + security critics (Medium). redeem() claims (consumes) the link before the owner==user check; the self-redeem branch skipped the grant AND the unredeem, returning success with the link consumed — so an owner testing their own link destroyed it for the intended recipient, contradicting the handler's 'self-redeem is a no-op success' comment. RESOLVED (server): the owner==user branch now unredeems (releases the claim), leaving the invite redeemable. Test: admin self_redeem_does_not_burn_the_link. Class: availability / single-use.

rows.title: Config first-contact direction is a whole-side overwrite with no preview, unlike the diff-showing conflict screens
rows.description: HF critique, Med (gulf of evaluation before commit). Turning on a config surface asks download/upload but shows nothing about what will change, while the more-recoverable per-file conflict shows a diff. PARTIALLY RESOLVED (1.6.0): the ConfigDirectionModal copy now sets expectations — 'only files that differ change, everything else is left alone, and later edits on either side reconcile normally'. NOTE: a true diff/count preview needs a local-vs-server compare the modal doesn't have; deferred as a possible follow-up. Class: pre-commit evaluation (copy-level mitigation).

rows.title: Fork/switch report progress only via a transient toast, lost when the app suspends
rows.description: HF critique, Med (gulf of evaluation for long ops). A fork/switch that uploads a whole vault can run for minutes; the modal closes and completion is a toast that fires into a suspended app, with only a generic yellow 'syncing' meanwhile — the user can't tell if it finished. RESOLVED (1.6.0): statusDisplay shows a persistent 'Switching vault…' state whenever a switch/fork is in flight, DERIVED from the saved pendingSwitch flag, so it survives suspend/resume and clears when the switch reconcile completes. Test: plugin-wiring statusDisplay pendingSwitch case. Class: long-op evaluation.

rows.title: No obsidian:// protocol handler — tapped share/setup links can't deep-link into the flow
rows.description: UX critique (IA lens), Medium. The plugin registers no registerObsidianProtocolHandler; share/setup payloads use bespoke selfsync:// / selfsync-share:// schemes the OS won't route into Obsidian, so every hand-off degrades to copy-paste. Fix would register an obsidian://selfsync?… handler that opens the setup-or-redeem flow prefilled, and re-encode payloads as obsidian:// URLs (keeping copyable text as fallback). DECLINED for now (larger change; deferred by wweatherholtz 2026-07-13). Class: onboarding friction (deferred).

rows.title: The pending-sync count includes remote files this device declined (config off / plugin not allowlisted) → a phantom count that never drains
rows.description: FIELD: reopening a vault showed 20+ pending syncs that 'never do anything'; the server log showed login OK then no transfers. Root cause: reconcileAll/reconcileDelta pre-classified the pending set from remote-vs-base WITHOUT applying the accepts() filter, so a remote file this device is set NOT to sync (a config surface off, or a community plugin not in the allowlist) was counted as pending even though reconcileOne correctly SKIPS it — it can never transfer, so the count never drained (and on mobile, which backgrounds mid-pass, it looked permanently stuck). The user also had no way to see WHAT was waiting or learn that plugin sync is opt-in on BOTH ends. RESOLVED (1.0.39): the pending pre-classifier now excludes accepts()-filtered files in both paths (honest 'work this device will do'); those files are surfaced via a new onDeclined callback → a coalesced, change-only log ('N community plugins / config files on the server are NOT in this device's sync selection — enable them in Settings → Obsidian configuration to sync them here'), which both explains the count and tells the user how to adopt a plugin another vault added. Test: reconcile 'does NOT count a remote file this device DECLINES as pending'. Class: misleading state / discoverability.

rows.title: Inbound sharing + conflicts are undiscoverable; redeem-while-signed-in ends in a toast that syncs nothing
rows.description: UX critique (IA + flows). Redeeming a share link — the primary INBOUND action — was reachable only by opening a button labelled 'Switch' and scrolling; a new recipient had no labelled path at all. Conflicts (data-safety, urgent) had no command/ribbon surface — only the transient toast + a settings section that exists only when conflicts are pending. And an already-signed-in redeem added the grant but relied on a 9s toast ('Open Settings → Switch vault to sync it') then synced NOTHING — easy to miss on mobile, so redeem looked like it did nothing. RESOLVED (1.5.0): added command-palette commands 'Switch vault', 'Redeem a share link', and 'Resolve conflicts' (routes to whichever kind is pending), renamed the setup command to 'Set up / reconfigure connection'; added a 'Redeem a share link' button to the unconfigured status card (the new-recipient entry point); and startRedeem now OPENS the Switch modal after an already-signed-in redeem (the redeemed vault is in its 'Shared with you' list) instead of leaving the second step to a toast. Class: discoverability / silent-until-later step.

rows.title: Four 'pick a side' surfaces use inconsistent wording + a biasing CTA on the unbiased note-conflict choice
rows.description: HF critique, Med (mental-model instability + capture error). The same 'which side wins?' decision was worded differently across note-conflict / config-conflict / config-direction / vault-switch, and the CTA (highlighted default) jumped sides — worst, the note-conflict highlighted 'Keep this device's' on a genuinely 50/50 IRREVERSIBLE content choice, inviting a reflexive tap that discards the other device's edits. RESOLVED (1.5.2): removed the CTA from the unbiased destructive choices (note-conflict + config-conflict); standardized config vocabulary to 'Use this device's' / 'Use the synced version'; CTA now reserved for a genuinely-safe default (vault-switch Merge). Class: mental-model consistency / capture-error prevention.

rows.title: UX polish: misdirecting recovery copy, jammed consent banner, silent max-file-size failure, inconsistent terminology + dead code
rows.description:
UX critique quick-win bundle. (MED) The setup server/consent banner used \ \ in a

with no white-space:pre-wrap, collapsing the compliance banner to one run-on line. (MED) 'Max file size' invalid/empty input failed SILENTLY — no save, no message, no revert. rows.title: Setup-wizard state is in-memory only — a mid-flow suspend can orphan a just-registered account
rows.description: UX critique (flows lens), Medium. The wizard keeps server/username/password/token in memory and persists only on finish; on mobile a suspend after 'Create account' registers the account server-side but reopening starts blank, so a second create attempt errors confusingly. Fix would persist wizard progress (at least server+username+registered-flag+token) or transition to a persisted logged-in state right after register. DECLINED for now (non-trivial; deferred by wweatherholtz 2026-07-13). Class: re-entrancy / mobile-suspend (deferred).

rows.title: merge3 didn't normalize CRLF → cross-platform edits exploded into spurious whole-file conflicts
rows.description: src/merge.ts splitLines() split on raw \ , leaving a trailing \\r on every CRLF line, so the LCS found ZERO common anchors between a CRLF base and an LF re-save — collapsing the whole file into one conflict region even when the real content edits didn't overlap. Obsidian vaults sync across Windows (CRLF) and macOS/Linux/mobile (LF), so this fired on nearly every cross-platform merge, undermining Merge as the 'nothing is lost' safe default in the vault-switch flow. Found by test/merge-eol.test.ts (authored it.fails, flipped to a passing regression on fix). FIX: normalize CRLF→LF before any comparison in merge3 (merged output already joins with \ , so this is consistent, not lossy). Severity Medium. discoveredInField=false — caught pre-release by the new merge suite.

rows.title: diagnose() read the throwing .json getter OUTSIDE its try/catch → a 200 with a non-JSON body threw out of the documented never-throws path
ContentStore::put fsync'd the blob bytes but not the shard DIR after rename → an acked commit's chunk could vanish on power loss
rows.description: chunkstore.rs put() did write-temp → sync_all(contents) → rename(tmp, p) but never fsync'd the containing shard directory after the rename. Its own R10-D1 invariant is explicit: a referenced chunk must survive power loss because the index (fsync'd on commit) points at it. sync_all makes the BYTES durable, but under POSIX the directory ENTRY created by the rename is not guaranteed to survive power loss without a parent-dir fsync. write_mirror (vault.rs) DOES perform exactly this dir-fsync and its comment claims parity with 'the chunk store' — which was false. Failure scenario: client puts chunk C (bytes fsync'd, renamed, dir-entry NOT fsync'd) → commits a file referencing C (index WAL fsync'd, durable) → server acks → power loss → on reboot the index durably cites C but its dir-entry was lost → verify_and_gc flags the dangling ref → reindex → classify_missing finds C gone → the file is lost → reindex aborts unless force. An acked commit's content unrecoverable — exactly what R10-D1 exists to prevent. Medium confidence on the practical window (ext4 data=ordered often carries the rename durably as a side effect; POSIX gives no guarantee, and the code elsewhere treats the dir-fsync as required). Found by the round-2 audit (chunkstore critic), verified against the code. FIX: fsync the shard dir (best-effort, File::open(dir).sync_all()) after the rename in put(), matching write_mirror so the two paths truly agree. Severity Medium. discoveredInField=false.

rows.title: index_store.migrate backfills the fold column with SQLite ASCII-only lower(), but the write path + colliding_key use Rust Unicode to_lowercase() → the case-collision guard misses legacy non-ASCII rows
rows.description: DI-1 (Medium). Healing a pre-fold DB backfills fold via `UPDATE files SET fold = lower(path)` (index_store.rs:100) — SQLite's bundled lower() is ASCII-ONLY — while every other producer/consumer uses Rust to_lowercase() (full Unicode): the write path (:154) and colliding_key's probe (:298-299). The comment at :291-295 even documents SQLite lower() is ASCII-only, so the backfill introduces exactly the write-path/guard drift :147-148 warns is 'a silent collision-guard hole'. Failure: an upgraded pre-fold DB holds 'CAFÉ.md'; migrate sets its fold='cafÉ.md' (É untouched). A later commit of 'café.md' probes fold='café.md' → no match → collision NOT detected → two keys folding to one file → on a case-insensitive client FS they collapse (PROTO-4/DI-R5 phantom-delete + overwrite churn). Narrow (needs an upgraded pre-fold DB with a non-ASCII-uppercase path never re-committed). FIX: backfill per-row in Rust with to_lowercase() (re-derive fold in migrate using the same fold as everywhere else). The existing migrate_heals test uses only ASCII 'A.md' so it can't catch this — add a non-ASCII case. Severity Medium. discoveredInField=false.

rows.title: pushBytes re-read the file from disk after writing merged bytes, so a racing local save was committed in place of the merge — silently dropping the remote edit
rows.description: CLIENT-2 (Medium, silent merge loss). pushBytes did io.write(mergedBytes) then pushFile, which RE-READ the file from disk (io.read) to chunk+commit. A user save landing in the write->read gap made pushFile commit the RACED content (local edit but NOT the remote edit the 3-way merge folded in) under the same server version (CAS doesn't protect — server didn't advance), setting base to it. DI-5 fixed base CONSISTENCY (text/hash agree) but not this LOSS of the merge result. Scenario: base 'L0\ R0'; peer→'L0\ R1', user→'L1\ R0'; merge3→'L1\ R1'; pushBytes writes it; user saves 'L1\ R0-edited' in the gap; pushFile commits that → the peer's R1 edit is gone fleet-wide. FIX: a shared commitBytes(ctx,path,bytes) core commits the IN-HAND bytes (no re-read); pushBytes writes to disk for local persistence then commits the merged bytes it holds, so a racing save is caught as a fresh local edit on the NEXT reconcile (local != base=merged → push/merge) instead of overwriting the merge. Fail-first test: pushBytes commits the exact bytes given, not the raced re-read. Severity Medium. discoveredInField=false.

rows.title: reconcilePath fed the coalesce-stale queued size into the symmetric size gate → a grow-then-shrink/delete was skipped until the full scan
doReconcileAll marked the config/full scan windows done BEFORE the awaited scan → a mid-scan failure skipped re-arming it
rows.description: main.ts doReconcileAll advanced lastConfigScanAt/lastFullScanAt to now up front, before await reconcileAll/reconcileDelta/reconcileLocalConfig. If any of those threw, the timestamps already claimed the scan happened, so a later poll wouldn't re-arm it — masked only because the throw routes to offline → doConnect, whose success re-stamps both; i.e. correctness leaned on the recovery path re-doing it rather than this function being self-consistent. Found by the round-2 audit (drivers critic), verified against the code. FIX: stamp the two windows AFTER the awaited scan completes, so a mid-scan failure leaves the window still due (the idle-poll early-return is only reached when NOT forced, so it correctly stamps nothing). Severity Low-Medium. discoveredInField=false.

rows.title: Share-LINKS survive vault/account deletion (only grants are purged), so a no-expiry link re-grants access across a delete+recreate boundary — the R17 remanence hole reopened for the link layer
rows.description: SEC-1 (Medium). purge_vault/purge_user_data (state.rs:257-287) and users_delete (admin.rs) meticulously drop share GRANTS (shares.purge_vault/purge_user, R17 — so a recreated same-name vault can't reactivate a grant) but NEVER touch .share-links.json; ShareLinkStore::open has no expiry sweep and links can be created with ttl=0 (no expiry); share_link_redeem mints the grant with no re-check that the owner still exists/owns the vault. Exploit: Alice creates a no-expiry ReadWrite link for alice/notes, hands/leaks the token, deletes vault notes (grants revoked — she reasonably believes access died), later recreates a vault named notes; Bob redeems the still-valid link → g.grant('alice','notes',bob,ReadWrite) → access to the recreated vault. Same across account delete + admin recreation of the username. FIX: add purge_links_for_vault(owner,vault) + purge_links_for_user(user) to ShareLinkStore, call them from the purge paths (mirror the shares.purge_* calls); add an open-time expiry sweep (parity with the tokens R22 sweep). Severity Medium. discoveredInField=false.

rows.title: ShareStore's persist-on-change deletions (revoke/purge_vault/purge_user) were asserted only in-memory → a save()-skip mutant survived (dropped grants would reload after a restart)
Vault::open's create_dir_all resurrects a just-deleted vault when it races a concurrent open past vault_exists()
rows.description: CONC-1 (Medium). state.rs vault() does NOT re-check existence — it unconditionally calls Vault::open, whose create_dir_all(vault_dir) (vault.rs:165) re-creates the tree. scoped() (api.rs) checks vault_exists() THEN spawn_blocking(st.vault()). Interleaving: request B passes vault_exists()==true, then its Vault::open create_dir_all runs AFTER request A's purge_vault remove_dir_all → the directory reappears empty and B caches a fresh empty VaultHandle → a just-deleted vault silently returns as an empty vault that vault_exists() now reports present (the server's delete is effectively undone; client empty-manifest guards prevent local data loss, but the delete didn't stick). FIX: serialize delete against open — hold the per-key opens lock across the purge (so no Vault::open runs for the key during teardown), and/or a 'deleting' tombstone set vault() consults before create_dir_all. Severity Medium. discoveredInField=false.

rows.title: vault.rs request path (commit/delete/safe_rel_path) had mutation-surfaced test gaps: integrity (right-size/wrong-hash), idempotency, version-bump, and path-safety were untested for their exact predicates
rows.description: cargo-mutants on vault.rs (the largest module): 95 caught / 33 survivors / 10 unviable = 74.2% over viable — the least mutation-covered module. 8 survivors were on the LIVE per-commit/delete request path (code correct; tests blind to the exact predicate): safe_rel_path's front guard `is_empty() || contains('\\') || starts_with('/')` had no test for an empty/absolute input (path-safety); commit's `req.size > MAX_FILE_BYTES` size gate was only tested with u64::MAX (both == and >= mutants survived — an over-limit request rerouted to a later mismatch error, or an at-limit request wrongly rejected); commit's integrity check `len != size || hash != claimed` — weakening the || would accept a right-SIZE/WRONG-HASH body (corruption laundered into a committed, served file); commit's idempotent short-circuit `hash == req.hash && chunks == req.chunks` — weakening the && would freeze a stale chunk list on a same-hash re-chunk; commit + delete `new_version = self.version + 1` — a `+1`->`*1` mutant stalls the version so peers never see the change/tombstone. FIX: 5 fail-first tests (safe_rel_path_rejects_empty_backslash_and_absolute, commit_size_gate_is_strict_greater_than, commit_rejects_correct_size_but_wrong_hash, commit_idempotency_requires_both_hash_and_chunks_to_match, commit_and_delete_each_bump_the_version). Confirming re-run: 102 caught / 26 missed (the 26 = 21 documented equivalent/impractical accepts + 5 reindex corrupt-rebuild gaps, issueVaultReindexRebuildTestGaps). Severity Medium (integrity + version-monotonicity + path-safety on the live write path; caught pre-release by mutation testing; no live defect). discoveredInField=false.

rows.title: The version counter lives only in the corruptible index and REWINDS on a quarantine/empty rebuild; history_floor is set BELOW already-synced client cursors, so the RC-1 conservative-reconcile never engages
rows.description: DI-3 (Medium). `version` lives only in the index meta table (index_store.rs:66-68 seeds 1 on a fresh/quarantined DB; vault.rs:185-189 quarantine→fresh). reindex rebuilds file versions from self.version (=1 after quarantine) up to max_version≈file count, then sets history_floor=max_version (vault.rs:411-429). For an active vault the pre-crash version M (total commits+deletes over its life) far exceeds the post-rebuild N≈file count, so M>>N is the COMMON outcome. A client synced at cursor M polls changes(since=M): gets version=N<M, empty upserts/deletes, history_floor=N. Per the floor semantics (only a client BELOW the floor reconciles conservatively) the client (cursor M>N) does NOT — a violated monotonicity invariant with no signal it can act on; the mechanism relied on for RC-1 is inert for the common rewind. Precise client-visible outcome depends on plugin reconcile (the client's version-rewind full-reconcile, issueVersionRewindPin, likely mitigates in practice — cross-check), but the server-side monotonicity break is certain. FIX: persist a monotonic high-water version OUTSIDE the corruptible index (a small fsync'd sidecar, bumped each commit) and seed the rebuilt index from it, so version never rewinds and the floor's below-floor semantics hold. Severity Medium. discoveredInField=false.

rows.title: Security bool-predicates (safe_name / isSafeVaultPath / isInsecureRemote) return bool not a refined type, forcing the checked property to be re-asserted at ~20 / 5 / 4 call sites (parse-don't-validate gap)
rows.description: parse-don't-validate conformance critic (verified). The weakness clusters in bool safety-predicates whose un-typed result forces defensive re-checking everywhere — exactly what the pattern eliminates: (1) safe_name (users.rs:28-37) is re-checked at ~20 call sites (admin.rs x10, state.rs x7, api.rs/vaults.rs/ws.rs/auth.rs) and DOUBLE-checked on the register write-path (auth.rs:136 then users.rs:133; state.rs:272 even comments 'the admin route already validated; defensive') — a name that reaches the FS as a path segment relies on every site remembering to call it; highest ROI. (2) isSafeVaultPath (pathsafe.ts:14-32) re-checked at 5 client I/O sites (main.ts write/read/exists/write/remove). (3) isInsecureRemote (connstr.ts:21-27) independently re-parses the raw URL via new URL() at 4 transport.ts sites, alongside (not consuming) normalizeServer's parse — shotgun parsing. FIX: a SafeName newtype (only ctor parses) taken by store keys/ns_dir/handlers; a branded SafeVaultPath taken by VaultIo read/write/remove (unchecked path → compile error); fold the insecure verdict into a refined ServerOrigin from normalizeServer. safe_rel_path (vault.rs, Option<PathBuf>, canonical round-trip, result trusted) is the reference parser to model on. Severity Medium (security-relevant reliance on human vigilance; no present bug). discoveredInField=false.

rows.title: The reconcile shells (reconcileOne/reconcileMergeOrConflict/reconcilePath) carry still-pure decision logic that should be lifted into explicit pure values (functional-core boundary too narrow)
rows.description: functional-core/imperative-shell conformance critic (verified). decide() is an EXEMPLARY pure total truth table (purity deliberately protected via requireRemote). But the three shells re-decide: (1) reconcileOne (reconcile.ts:780-947) delegates the 3-way call to decide() then adds a SECOND layer of largely-pure decision logic in the shell — config re-adjudication (848-858), delete gating on hasTombstone/guardDelete/guardRemoteDelete (897,910,921,929), size gate (792-798). Lift into a pure finalize(action, facts)→Effect (resolve confirmedAbsent/exists to booleans in the shell first); the switch then only executes Effects. (2) reconcileMergeOrConflict (700-760) uses the pure kernels (merge3/sameIgnoringEol/isMergeable) but interleaves outcome selection with I/O (partly inherent) — compute a pure MergePlan value, shell executes writes. (3) reconcilePath (617-657) inlines the delete-guard denominator/wouldDelete (626-641), duplicating runDeleteGuard (220-226, the B1 drift) — extract a shared perPassDeleteGuard(d, manifest) helper used by all three entry points. Net: widen the property-testable pure boundary. Severity Medium (design/testability; no correctness bug). discoveredInField=false.

rows.title: check-release/verify-released (D0012) only assert the MANIFEST's version is released — unreleased SHIPPABLE commits piling up on main (manifest left at an already-released version) are invisible
rows.description: The owner asked why 99 commits had accumulated on main since 1.6.0 with no release, despite D0012 adding check-release.mjs + verify-released.yml specifically to make 'released' a checkable assertion. Root cause: those checks assert only that MANIFEST.json's version has a matching tag + published GitHub release — a condition SATISFIED the entire time, because the manifest sat at 1.6.0 (which WAS released) while main drifted 99 commits (48 of them touching shippable client/server/manifest paths; 52 engine/tracking/docs-only) past it. So D0012 catches 'bumped-but-never-tagged' (the 0.10.4 miss) but is BLIND to 'never-bumped-so-work-accrues-unreleased' — a distinct drift. This violated D0002 ('every coherent set of committed, green changes ships as a version increment') for ~a week across the mutation/critique/pattern sittings, undetected. FIX (releaseCurrencyGuard): a repo-local scripts/check-release-currency.mjs (mirroring D0012's out-of-keel-scope pattern) that counts main commits since the last release tag touching SHIPPABLE paths only (so tracking/engine/docs commits don't false-positive), WARNs at >=1 and FAILs past a threshold, wired into verify-released.yml. Severity Medium (a process-control gap that already caused a real week-long release lapse; no user-facing defect). discoveredInField=false.

rows.title: The 2 tagged sync FSMs are correct but DEAD (only the test uses them); the live operational machine is a hybrid, and ~4 IMPLICIT FSMs (WS lifecycle, engine, reconcile-mode, config-adjudication) are boolean-soup that should be explicit
rows.description: actor/state-machine conformance critic (verified by grep + read). This answers 'why only 2 state machines?': (a) syncstate::transition + SyncMachine (syncstate.ts) are CORRECT total (State,Event)→State machines but ORPHANED — imported only by client/test/syncstate.test.ts; the operational machine migrated to syncengine.ts, whose header says the old FSM 'only ever drove the status LIGHT'. So the 2 tagged FSMs model nothing live. (b) The LIVE engine (SyncEngine, syncengine.ts) is a HYBRID: an explicit EngineState enum + 3 aux booleans (connected/retrying/running) + IMPERATIVE transitions in handle() — not a total transition table. (c) IMPLICIT FSMs that should be explicit, by value: D1 WS/transport lifecycle (main.ts spinUpWs/startWsLiveness/close-handler — realtimeConnected/opened/`ws!==ws`/poll-cadence/wsLivenessTimer encode no-socket/dialing/open/half-open-stale/closed-redial/closed-reconnect, with a documented history of race patches CONC-R2#4/#6/CONC-R3#1/R11#7 → strongest case for an explicit TransportState machine); D4 the engine hybrid; D2 doReconcileAll scan-mode (4 booleans → 4 modes); D3 config-path adjudication (array-membership-as-state). The (serialized-actor) SyncEngine.pump/handle ARE strong (real queue, run-to-completion, owned state) — the FSM issue is the transition MODELING, not the actor. Resolve via stateMachineConsolidation (delete-or-reunify the orphans; make the implicit machines explicit, model = decide()). Severity Medium (clarity/testability + a race-patch-prone lifecycle; no present bug). discoveredInField=false.

rows.title: validateFileMeta asserts mtime:number in its return type but never validates it — a hostile server's non-numeric mtime passes and flows into base stat-stamping
rows.description: DEFECT (Medium), surfaced by the parse-don't-validate conformance critic + VERIFIED. protocol.ts:49-57 validateFileMeta validates path/hash/size/version (asStr/asNum) + chunks (string[]) but has NO check for mtime, then returns `o as FileMeta` (line 56) — the FileMeta type (protocol.ts) asserts mtime:number. So a malformed/hostile server response with mtime:'evil' / NaN / missing passes validation and is cast to FileMeta; mtime flows into live base stat-stamping (reconcile localStat/stampStat paths). The exact parse-don't-validate hazard: the refined type promises a property the parser doesn't establish. Contrast validateStatus (protocol.ts:61-72), which CONSTRUCTS a fresh normalized value (the true exemplar). FIX: add asNum(m.mtime, 'mtime') and construct-don't-cast (build + return a fresh FileMeta). Severity Medium (untrusted-input validation hole; the client already re-hashes downloaded CONTENT so this is metadata-integrity, not content-loss). discoveredInField=false (critique).

rows.title: Vault's corrupt + dangling_recovery bool pair is an IMPLICIT lifecycle FSM (Ok/Corrupt/DanglingRecovery) that can even represent an illegal state — should be an explicit enum VaultState
Sync raises conflicts/merges for timestamp-only frontmatter differences — the whole file is hashed, so any updated: bump reads as a content change
rows.description: Owner-reported on real devices: 'wayy too many diff conflicts that are just time metadata with no file changes otherwise.' Root cause: change detection hashes the ENTIRE file byte-for-byte (reconcile.ts sha256hex), frontmatter included, with zero frontmatter awareness — so when a note's embedded modified/created timestamp differs across devices (a copy, a re-open, or an editor-event plugin re-stamp) while the body is identical, the hashes differ and decide() routes it to merge / conflict-copy. FIX (embeddedTimestampMetadata sprint): SelfSync owns the updated/created fields and compares by a NORMALIZED content hash that masks the managed timestamp keys (git-model content-addressing), so a timestamp-only difference is a non-event; a spurious local bump is reverted-not-pushed, and a genuine timestamp-only cross-device diff auto-resolves keeping the older updated / earliest created — no conflict copy. Severity Medium (no data loss, but a chronic false-conflict UX defect). discoveredInField=true (owner, real devices).

rows.title: Enabling embedded timestamps did nothing visible — feature was lazy (stamped only on next edit), so a settled vault saw no effect + no kickoff
rows.description: Owner-reported after 1.7.0: 'embed created/updated timestamps doesn't make it clear when it's actually processing — it doesn't seem to be doing.' The feature stamped a note only on its next GENUINE EDIT; an already-synced/settled vault took the in-sync path and was never stamped, so flipping the toggle produced zero observable effect and there was no instantiation/kickoff. FIX (timestampBackfill, 1.8.0): a convergence pass on enable / policy-change / settled-launch that brings every in-scope .md note to compliance (seed from OS metadata, normalize non-canonical — instant-based, never bumps), paced + resumable via a per-vault marker/cursor, reversible via a conflict-copy for any not-cleanly-conformable note, gated by an informed COUNTED confirm with restore-signature detection; third-party alias keys masked in identity (no Linter re-stamp storm); Templates folder excluded. Severity Medium (usability — the feature appeared inert). discoveredInField=true (owner).

rows.title: Embedded-timestamp v-next hardening: honor manual managed-field edits (F9), scan-skip vs external mtime-preserving tools (F12), DST-correct offset labels (F14), >1MiB churn-killer gap (F15)
rows.description: Deferred (non-ship-blocking) findings from the embeddedTimestampMetadata pre-release critique: F9 (MEDIUM) the copy/re-stamp revert blind-restores base.text, so a user's manual correction of a managed created/updated is reverted every sync — should reconcile the managed fields (honor an earlier/legit value) instead; F12 (MED-LOW) driving FS mtime to the embedded updated weakens the scan-skip's 'a write bumps mtime' premise, so a body-only change by an external mtime-preserving tool (rsync -a) could be missed until a full scan — niche mixed-sync-tool setups; F14 (LOW) formatIsoOffset uses the CURRENT tz offset for a historically-stamped time, mislabeling by the DST delta (instant still correct, only the human offset is off); F15 (LOW/MED) a >1MiB managed note whose base text is dropped (MAX_BASE_TEXT_BYTES) skips the churn-killer revert and gets a spurious updated=now on a mere copy (bounded — converges after one push via persisted normHash). discoveredInField=false (critique-found). MOOTED 2026-08-01 by timestampIgnoreRedesign (1.9.0): all four findings targeted the 'SelfSync owns created/updated' code path — the copy/re-stamp revert (F9/F15), driving FS mtime to the embedded updated (F12), and formatIsoOffset (F14) — ALL of which the redesign DELETED (SelfSync now writes no note timestamps; identity masks timestamp-valued keys instead). With no stamping/revert/fs-mtime-drive code left, none of F9/F12/F14/F15 has a subject. Resolver repointed from the never-started embeddedTimestampHardening action to the completed redesign.

rows.title: CRLF/BOM-only differences are flagged as content changes — normalizedHash short-circuited to the RAW hash for a note without frontmatter (a SEPARATE root cause from timestamps)
rows.description: Owner-reported: 'TONS of false positives that incorrectly identify changes when none really exists (CR/LF issues?).' An independent design-fit critic confirmed this is a DISTINCT root cause from the timestamp noise: normalizedHash (frontmatter.ts) returned the RAW byte hash for any note WITHOUT frontmatter (hasFrontmatter false -> sha256hex(bytes)), so EOL/BOM normalization never ran on plain notes and a CRLF↔LF re-save read as a content change; and even for notes with frontmatter the EOL normalization was gated behind the (feature-on) path. FIX (timestampIgnoreRedesign, 1.9.0): content identity ALWAYS normalizes EOL/BOM/trailing-newline for ALL text files, independent of the timestamp feature (the no-frontmatter short-circuit removed), and a cosmetic-only local change is recognized in-sync (not pushed) via the post-decide normHash override. Guard: the CRLF-only-not-pushed reconcile test + plain-note EOL identity tests. Severity Medium (chronic false-conflict/churn UX defect; no data loss). discoveredInField=true.

rows.title: A plugin the user removed still shows as 'synced' — server plugin FILES are never pruned and community-plugins.json is grow-only, so a removal never propagates
rows.description: Owner-reported: 'update-time-on-edit shows up in the synced community plugins' though not installed; 'there should be absolute parity here.' Root cause (verified): (A) the synced-plugins list is a UNION of local manifests + getServerPluginIds(); getServerPluginIds is derived by regex over EVERY remote file path (reconcile.ts onRemotePlugins), so it = every plugin with ANY file on the server. (B) removal never propagates: setPluginSync(id,false) only drops the id from pluginAllow (deletes nothing); then shouldSync=false -> the accepts predicate skips those paths ENTIRELY (no pull, no base, NO delete-remote), so the server folder lingers forever. (C) community-plugins.json is a deliberately grow-only union (mergeEnabledPluginsJson: enables propagate, disables do not, reconcile.ts:806-807), so the id is re-added every sync and never removed — why the vault still lists it enabled. FIX (pluginSyncRemovalPropagation): UI split (available-to-adopt vs synced) + a sanctioned removal channel (delete-remote for the plugin folder + a removal op the enabled-list merge honors) — a CHANGE to the catastrophe-proof-asymmetric merge, needs a Decision. Severity Medium. discoveredInField=true.

rows.title: Connection-FSM Medium/Low follow-ups: LinkState not reset on disconnect (stale vault-gone prompt), serverDegraded reindex message clobbered, MFA/must-change-pw body-string classification, dead UserRetry edge / 429 re-arm / 503 retry-after
rows.description: FSM critic Medium/Low findings (verified), backlogged behind the 3 HIGH fixes: F2 disconnect/unload leave LinkState so getLastIssue/isVaultGone leak a stale blocked/vault-gone prompt after disconnect; F3 the actionable serverDegraded 'run reindex' message is overwritten by the generic outer catch and shows 'Reconnecting…'; F4 MFA/must-change-password classification matches un-pinned server body strings; F5 the UserRetry LinkState edge is dead, a repeated 429 re-arms retryAfter each cycle, and Retry-After is honored only for 429. discoveredInField=false (critique-found).

rows.title: Security Medium/Low follow-ups: hot-load privacy gate trusts SERVER-reported share metadata (malicious-server threat — needs an owner decision); removePluginFromServer id not validated + re-push re-hot-loads
rows.description: Security critic Medium/Low findings (verified): S2 (threat-model decision) vaultIsPrivate is derived from share metadata the SERVER reports, and that same server ships the plugin bytes — a compromised/hostile server could lie 'not shared' -> hot-load. In scope only if the self-hosted server is treated as untrusted; needs an owner decision (accept-risk vs client-side attestation vs revert the private-vault hot-load exception). S3 (LOW) removePluginFromServer(id) builds a delete prefix from a server/peer-influenced id with no validation (reject `..`/`/`/empty); a removed plugin re-pushed by another active device re-arrives and, on a private vault, hot-loads again without re-approval. discoveredInField=false (critique-found).

rows.title: Timestamp content-identity Medium/Low follow-ups: Date.parse value-shape gate over-masks bare-year/manual dates (contradicts the UI promise) + non-portable V8/JSCore; trailing-newline inconsistency; normHash never written
rows.description: Timestamp critic Medium/Low findings (verified), on the DEFAULT-ON feature so wide blast radius. T1 the isTimestampValue gate uses Date.parse, so a bare-year `created: 2020` (or a manually-curated date) is masked -> editing it silently doesn't propagate, contradicting the settings UI's 'a non-date value under the same key still syncs'. T2 Date.parse is engine-defined -> a non-canonical value hashes differently on desktop V8 vs mobile JSCore -> cross-platform churn. T4 trailing-newline normalization differs between normalizedContent (collapse 2+->1) and merge3's sameIgnoringEol (strip all) -> a final-newline toggle churns; lone-CR not normalized. T3 normHash is declared/serialized/read but never written (override rides on base.text recompute; >1MiB gap documented-accepted). discoveredInField=false (critique-found).

rows.title: Vault-change Medium/Low follow-ups: redeem + owner-axis + guard-driven changes bypass the resolution modal (silent merge = cross-vault union); empty-base guard skip; fire-and-forget key stamp
rows.description: Vault-change critic Medium/Low findings (verified): V2 setupwizard finishRedeem + the direct-adopt path reconnect() with NO resolution modal (only the vaultId-name axis was closed), and the guard's remedy is a SILENT merge (a union across two vaults = contamination) rather than the Download/Upload/Cancel adjudication SwitchVaultModal offers — route guard-detected changes through the same modal. V3 the guard requires base.paths().length so a vault change with an empty base but local files skips it (pushes local into the new vault); baseVaultKey is stamped via a fire-and-forget save. discoveredInField=false (critique-found).

rows.title: The .obsidian config-tree enumeration is fully sequential — a plugin-heavy tree costs many seconds on a latency-bound (mobile) adapter, every reconcile
rows.description: Owner-reported via the 1.12.0 connect timing: the 'scanning local files' phase took ~18s (2.5s -> 20.5s in the log), before the reconcile even started. Root cause: ObsidianVaultIo.enumerateConfig walked the hidden .obsidian/ tree FULLY SEQUENTIALLY — one awaited adapter.list(dir) per directory + one awaited adapter.stat(file) per passing file, depth-first — so the wall-clock was (call COUNT x per-call latency). The notes come from Obsidian's in-memory getFiles() instantly; only this config walk does async fs work, and it runs on EVERY reconcile (incl. polls), not just connect. On mobile (Android — the owner's device) each adapter call round-trips a filesystem bridge, so a plugin-heavy .obsidian tree (many plugin dirs/files) = seconds. OWNER DIRECTED the fix ('then the other'). FIX (configWalkParallel 1.12.4): extract the walk into a pure, unit-tested configwalk.ts (walkConfigTree) that runs adapter.list/stat CONCURRENTLY under a GLOBAL concurrency cap (a counting semaphore — a per-call mapPool can't bound a recursive walk), collapsing the wall-clock toward (tree DEPTH x latency). Read-only + behavior-preserving: it finds exactly the same passing-file set (order-independent), a dir it can't list is SKIPPED (not treated as empty — reconcile's per-file probe still guards a false delete) + logged, and a slow walk logs its shape ('config scan: N folders + M files in Xs') so the effect is measurable. Guards: configwalk.test — finds every passing file across a nested tree; respects the passes filter; a list error skips only that subtree + continues; NEVER exceeds the global cap (peak<=limit) yet DID run in parallel (peak>1); empty tree. discoveredInField=true (owner). Severity Medium (perf; every-reconcile cost, worse on mobile).

rows.title: 'Connecting…' is one opaque label over several phases with no sub-phase or timing — a slow phase reads as hung with zero insight (L-5)
rows.description: Owner-reported (field): the status hung on 'connecting' with no insight into why; the log showed 'connecting to ... as will' then a 36s gap then 'config sync on — syncing 38 files' and nothing between. doConnect (main.ts) runs THREE phases all labeled 'Connecting…' and logs NOTHING between them on the happy path: (1) establishSession — acquireToken (login/cached) -> api.status() first authed round-trip (30s timeout) -> version handshake -> refreshShareGrant; (2) resolveAndApplySwitch -> reconcileFull -> reconcileAll — which fetches the FULL remote manifest (changes(0)) THEN lists+hashes every local file (the 'config sync on' log is emitted by io.list, so the 36s of silence was establishSession + the manifest fetch, BEFORE the local scan even started); (3) finishConnect — WS + poll. By design (connectPhaseNoOptimisticFlip 1.11.5) the status stays 'Connecting…' through the whole initial reconcile and only flips to 'Syncing…' on real transfer work — good against a false 'Synced', but it makes a slow initial scan/fetch look hung. The user (a controller) can't tell a slow connect from a stuck one and has no timing to locate the stall — an L-5 inadequate-feedback gap on the connect control loop (parallels S-14, the no-progress bulk op). RESOLUTION (owner directed 'Status sub-phases + timed log'): connectPhaseVisibility (1.12.0) names each sub-phase (signing in / checking the server / checking your access / fetching changes / scanning local files / reconciling N) as the 'Connecting…' DETAIL (card/tooltip) AND logs each with cumulative elapsed, driven by a new reconcile onStage hook + a connect-gated setConnectStage. discoveredInField=true (owner). Severity Medium (misleading/opaque, not data loss).

rows.title: The 'Diagnose' button gives a FALSE 'all good' — it probes only the connection chain, blind to whether sync is actually converging (L-5 misleading UX)
rows.description: Owner-reported. HttpTransport.diagnose walked the CONNECTION chain (reachable -> version -> auth -> vault present -> server-index-not-degraded) via fresh out-of-band HTTP probes and returned 'All good' when all five links were healthy. But it NEVER consulted the live sync engine (getState/linkState/getPhase/pending, per-file retry budget), so it was structurally blind to sync NON-convergence: a stalled/off engine, pending work not draining, a file looping on an error, or a wedged FSM. So exactly when sync is stuck-but-the-pipe-is-fine — the case the user clicks Diagnose for — it falsely says 'everything is fine' (an L-5 misleading feedback, feeding a wrong picture into the USER's process model; relates to H-9 reported!=actual). Worse: it was a SECOND, out-of-band source of truth that could CONTRADICT the honest status card (a pure FSM projection) built this sitting — the dual-source anti-pattern the status-FSM work exists to kill. Analysis showed the honest status card already surfaces every actionable cause diagnose gave, via connstate.blockedTip (version mismatch / sign-in rejected / session expired / MFA / vault-gone / access-removed / degraded) derived from REAL sync failures. RESOLUTION (owner-directed 'consider just removing'): REMOVE the Diagnose button + its chain (removeDiagnoseButton, 1.11.11) so the honest FSM-projected status line is the SINGLE source of truth (it cannot give a false all-clear because it is a pure projection). discoveredInField=true (owner). Severity Medium (misleading, not data loss).

rows.title: MFA-enrolled accounts can't sign in via the plugin — login sends no TOTP code and the wizard/reconfigure has no field for one
The connect examination shows a static 'reconciling N files' — overstates (implies syncing) AND looks stuck when the pass is slow, with no progress
rows.description: Owner-reported (field): the connect status showed 'reconciling 1137 local file(s)' and appeared to do nothing ('says reconciling but not doing anything'), then 'stuck on label'. Two problems: (1) LABEL — my connect sub-phase (1.12.0) said 'reconciling N local file(s)', which reads as 'syncing N' when the pass actually EXAMINES all files to detect changes and transfers only what CHANGED (nothing changed -> 0 work -> completes to Fully synced). (2) NO PROGRESS — the examination showed a STATIC label, so a SLOW full pass (a first-run re-hash before the 1.12.2 scan-skip stamps have persisted; or a large mobile vault) looks frozen, and a genuine hang is indistinguishable from slow. The engine can't flip to 'Fully synced' until reconcileAll returns, so a slow/hung pass leaves the connect on the stale label. FIX (reconcileExamProgress 1.12.5): (a) honest label 'checking N files for changes' (examines, not syncs; real transfer work still shows as 'Syncing… N pending' via onProgress); (b) LIVE progress 'checked X/N files' (every 250 examined) so a slow pass shows MOVEMENT (not fake-stuck) and a genuine hang is PINPOINTED — the count freezes at the stuck file. NOTE: this is a UX + DIAGNOSTIC fix; if the underlying stall is a hard hang (not a one-time slow re-hash that completes + persists stamps), the frozen progress count locates it for a targeted follow-up. Guards: reconcile.test onStage sequence updated (fetching -> scanning -> 'checking N files for changes'). discoveredInField=true (owner). Severity Medium (misleading + looks-stuck; the connect blocks on the examination).

rows.title: Every plugin reload re-reads + re-hashes the WHOLE vault on the first connect — the size/mtime scan-skip hint was deliberately not persisted
rows.description: Owner-reported via the 1.12.0 connect timing: on a fresh 'plugin loaded' the first connect reconciles ~1137 files though nothing changed and it was fully synced. Root cause: the (size,mtime) scan-skip hint (which lets a whole-vault reconcile skip the read+SHA-256 of an unchanged file) was DELIBERATELY in-memory-only — BaseStore.toJSON (base.ts) persisted only hash/text/normHash, dropping size/mtime ('never let a perf hint outlive its verifying session', R15 sync#3). So after every reload the base has no stamps, baseStatUnchanged can't match, and reconcileOne re-reads+re-hashes every file (nothing transfers — still fully synced — but it re-does the verification, the field cost). Also surfaced by the same log: the ~18s pre-reconcile is io.list() walking the whole .obsidian config tree (SEPARATE issue, not this one), and 'token rejected — re-logging in' every connect (session token not reused; separate). OWNER DECISION (AskUserQuestion 'Persist the scan-skip hints'): persist size+mtime in toJSON so a reload trusts the same rsync/Syncthing (size,mtime) heuristic the in-session skip already uses. TRADEOFF (independent critic verified SOUND — no data-loss path): a file changed OUT of Obsidian while off, preserving BOTH size AND mtime, isn't re-hashed on reload — the exact accepted rsync residual, now WIDER (the reload full-rehash backstop is removed, so the rare miss self-heals only on the next edit event / size|mtime change / remote divergence, not on the next restart). It is a DELAYED push, NEVER data loss (a lying stamp colliding with a remote change re-reads live in applyPull->conflictCopyIfRaced and writes a conflict copy — never a silent overwrite), and never hides a REMOTE change (detected via the manifest). FIX (persistScanSkipHint 1.12.2): toJSON emits size+mtime (constructor already loads them); guarded by base.test (round-trip) + reconcile T2/T5 (unchanged skips read + noop), T3 (stale stamp still re-reads a change), T4 (lying stamp + remote divergence -> conflict copy, the safety test), T6 (absent file not masked -> delete-remote fires), and a main.ts mtime-source-parity invariant (T7). discoveredInField=true (owner). Severity Medium (perf/UX; unrecoverable-loss ruled out by the critic).

rows.title: A mid-stream local edit is silently, unrecoverably lost on a large-file (>=8 MiB) streamed pull — the buffered path is safe, the streamed path was not (L-1)
rows.description: Client chunking/reassembly STPA-UCA hunt finding (UCA-4 / S-3 / SR-2 family). applyPull's streamed branch (rmeta.size >= STREAM_MIN_BYTES, 8 MiB) ran the racing-edit check (conflictCopyIfRaced) BEFORE streaming, then streamFileToDisk reassembled to a temp file and atomic-renamed it over `path` in close() with NO re-check in the seam. So an edit saved to that file DURING the multi-second download was clobbered by the rename, and base was set to the remote hash → next reconcile sees local==base → in-sync → the edit is gone, unrecoverably. The BUFFERED path (all files < 8 MiB) is SAFE — it re-checks AFTER the fetch (reconcile.ts). Asymmetry: small notes protected, large files (e.g. a live-edited >8 MiB .canvas) not. This was EXACTLY SR-2's documented 'Residual (accepted): a sub-window TOCTOU on very large streamed pulls.' Prior attempts to close it regressed (a 'post-write re-read' that read the file AFTER the rename = remote bytes, laundering wrong bytes into base) — so the fix needed care. FIX (streamedPullRacingEditGuard 1.12.1): streamFileToDisk gains a beforeRename hook called after the incremental hash-verify + before close()'s rename; applyPull passes a seam guard that reuses conflictCopyIfRaced on the ORIGINAL on-disk file (which still holds the racing edit — never the post-rename result, so base is only ever rmeta.hash). An independent critic (SOUND-WITH-CHANGES) caught a follow-on hole: the orphan-cleanup would delete the SOLE surviving racing edit if close() throws AFTER the rename applied — so the fix does NOT delete the seam copy on failure (a redundant copy is cosmetic; a deleted edit is loss), plus a close()-must-never-throw-after-rename contract. Guards (fail-first): reconcile.test 'preserves a mid-stream local edit as a conflict copy', 'makes NO spurious copy when there is no racing edit', 'a >8 MiB config file ... ABORTS (adjudicate)', 'a close() failure AFTER the rename does NOT delete the sole surviving racing edit'. discoveredInField=false (STPA-hunt-found). Severity Medium (narrow window — >=8 MiB files hand-edited mid-download; unrecoverable but rare; notes unaffected).

rows.title: A vault switch (upload/download) reports no progress, so it sits on a static 'Connecting…' and looks hung during a long transfer
rows.description: After connectPhaseNoOptimisticFlip (1.11.5) the card honestly showed 'Connecting…' during the initial reconcile, but the owner reported it looked 'hung on connecting?' during a persisted 'upload' switch. Root cause: the normal reconcile (reconcileAll) reports onProgress (a decrementing pending count), but switchTo/switchUpload/switchDownload reported NONE — so syncPending stayed 0, there was no 'Syncing… N' detail and no state escalation, and a long/large switch sat on a static 'Connecting…'. FIX (switchReportsProgress, 1.11.6): switchDownload + switchUpload report onProgress like reconcileAll (full count up front, decrement to 0) — so an active switch shows 'Syncing… N pending' decreasing, a stalled one a stuck count, and an outage still aborts to 'Reconnecting…'. discoveredInField=true (owner, mobile). NOTE: the underlying block remains that notes2.willweatherholtz.com is unreachable (the owner's server/DNS).

rows.title: Untrusted CSS (theme/snippet) synced from a shared vault is applied with only a restart notice — no trust warning, no private-vault gate, unlike plugin code (L-3)
rows.description: STPA-UCA hunt finding (caApplyConfig, L-3, Medium): flushConfigReload classifies synced themes/snippets/appearance CSS as 'will apply after restart' (a bare Notice) on the premise that CSS is 'never auto-applied' — but the plugin WRITES the CSS to disk during reconcile, and Obsidian hot-reloads an ENABLED snippet/theme on file change without a restart. On a readWrite-shared vault (snippets default ON) a peer can overwrite an enabled snippet's .css and Obsidian applies it live; CSS in Obsidian's un-CSP'd renderer enables exfil (background:url(...)) + phishing overlays (a class the code's own comment acknowledges). UCA-7 NAMES CSS but its realized mitigation SR-5 gates only plugin CODE (the restart trust-barrier + private-vault hot-load); CSS gets neither the trust warning nor the private-vault gate. Partly accepted-by-parity with Obsidian Sync (which also applies synced snippets) — so this NEEDS AN OWNER DECISION (gate/trust-warn untrusted shared-vault CSS vs accept-by-parity), not a unilateral fix. discoveredInField=false (STPA-hunt-found). Separately, the hunt re-confirmed the accepted S2 malicious-server oracle risk (issueSecurityHardeningBacklog) and sharpened it (the codebase elsewhere defends against a compromised server) — noted for the owner's re-weighing, already accept-risk'd.

rows.title: The WS open/error handlers lack the superseded-socket identity guard that close has — a late error from an OLD socket degrades the CURRENT live socket
rows.description: Client WS-push STPA-UCA hunt finding (Medium). spinUpWs supersedes a socket by this.ws?.close() then pointing this.ws at the new one; the FSM design (transportstate.ts:7) requires ALL socket events to honor the this.ws!==ws identity check. The `close` handler and the liveness tick DO guard, but `open` (main.ts) and `error` did NOT. So a late `error` from a SUPERSEDED old socket (racing the abort supersession triggers) called applyTransport('errored') -> transportTransition(live,'errored') -> degraded -> the CURRENT live socket is forced to degraded: realtimeConnected reads false, the light shows yellow 'Synced (polling)' instead of green 'Fully synced', and the poll is pinned to POLL_ACTIVE_MS (4s) until the next full socket cycle (battery). SAFE direction (under-claims health; changes still flow via the poll -> no missed changes, no false-synced), so Medium not High; a clear bug (asymmetric guard contradicting the FSM's own supersession design). The dangerous direction (a stale `open` flipping to false-live) is unreachable (supersession close()s a still-connecting socket, which aborts without firing open) but the open guard is added for symmetry. FIX (wsSupersededGuard 1.12.6): add `if (this.unloading || !this.api || this.ws !== ws) return;` to both open + error handlers, matching close. Guard: plugin-wiring 'a SUPERSEDED WS socket's late open/error does NOT disturb the current live socket' (fail-first). discoveredInField=false (WS-hunt-found). Severity Medium (wrong status light + battery; no data risk).

rows.title: Moving a file OUT of a SYNC-mount folder deletes it from the (possibly another user's) SOURCE vault, and moving one IN removes it from the primary — correct sync semantics but a surprising, unconfirmed cross-boundary data flow
rows.description: Surfaced by hardening Round 5 (security/holistic critique, finding MED-2). A composed mount and the primary are disjoint scopes. Dragging a note OUT of a sync-mount folder (e.g. Work/ASI/note.md → Notes/note.md): the primary sees a create of the new path (fine); the mount sees Work/ASI/note.md become locally-absent with base+remote present → delete-local → on a SYNC mount that propagates as a delete-REMOTE to the source vault, removing the file from another user's shared vault. Moving one IN is the mirror (removed from the primary server, pushed to the source). It is TECHNICALLY CORRECT sync (the file left/entered the synced folder), and a single-file delete is below BULK_DELETE_RATIO so the delete-guard doesn't catch it — but it crosses a trust boundary from an innocuous local reorganization, without a rename/move detection or a confirmation. Only affects SYNC mounts (opt-in + warned; a PULL mount never pushes/deletes the source). MITIGATION now: documented as expected behavior in the sync-mount warning path; FULL FIX (follow-up): lightweight rename/move detection across the mount boundary, or a confirmation before a mount-driven delete-remote of a non-tombstoned file. discoveredInField=false (critique-found). Severity Medium (cross-user data deletion from an ordinary local move on a sync mount; bounded to opt-in sync mounts, semantically-correct, not a breach).

rows.title: A composed-vault SYNC mount does not run D0019 deletion-history-reset detection (reset hardcoded false, onKeptAbsent only logged), so it could resurrect a peer's deleted file into the shared source on a source history prune
rows.description: Surfaced by hardening Round 2 (data-integrity critique, finding F3). The primary sync computes a `reset` from the server's history_floor (D0019) and batches onKeptAbsent for user review; the mount sync loop (mountsync.ts) hardcodes reset:false. So on a SYNC mount, if the SOURCE vault prunes its deletion history past a file's tombstone, a local-present/base-present/remote-absent/no-tombstone file takes the restore (keep+push) path and RE-UPLOADS a file the source owner deleted, back into the shared source. R2 MITIGATED the SILENCE by wiring onKeptAbsent (a toast + log) so the keep/restore is now visible, not silent — and a PULL mount cannot resurrect at all (read-only). The residual (unfixed) is the AUTOMATIC re-upload on a sync mount under a source history reset. FULL FIX: port D0019 to the mount — persist a per-mount history floor + last-version (like the primary's historyFloors, keyed by mountKey), detect a reset from the mount's ChangesResponse.history_floor, and on a suspected reset route kept-absent files to a user-reviewed batch instead of auto-restoring. Low probability (needs a source-side history prune past the horizon + a sync mount holding the file) + now visible via onKeptAbsent, so tracked as a follow-up rather than a v1 blocker. discoveredInField=false (critique-found). Severity Medium (data resurrection into a shared resource on a sync mount; bounded + now-visible).

rows.title: The bulk-delete guard is whole-vault-calibrated; on a small composed-vault mount SUBTREE it both over-blocks normal source deletions (mount never converges) and under-protects tiny mounts — a calibration/safety-posture decision
rows.description: Surfaced by hardening Round 9 (reconcile-engine-reuse critique, finding A). The shared reconcile bulk-delete guard (runDeleteGuard: acceptedBasePaths as the universe + the filtered manifest, BULK_DELETE_MIN=6 / BULK_DELETE_RATIO=0.5 + the empty-manifest override) is calibrated for a WHOLE VAULT, where an empty/high-ratio-delete manifest is a strong index-loss/attack signal. For a MOUNT SUBTREE those are NORMAL user actions, producing THREE mismatches: (1) empty-manifest override — a user emptying the mounted source folder makes remote.size===0 trip the override → every delete-local refused (reportGuard) → the mount keeps the deleted files forever, never mirrors the emptying; (2) RATIO=0.5 — deleting ≥half of a ≥6-file mount (routine for a small folder) trips guardBulkDelete → refused / non-convergent; (3) tiny mounts (<6 files) get NO ratio guard AND the cumulative DeleteRateGuard early-returns, so a partial drain is unguarded. This is a genuine SAFETY-POSTURE tradeoff — how aggressively should a mount propagate deletions from its source? — NOT a clear-cut bug, so it is SURFACED for the maintainer's decision rather than unilaterally changed (deletes are recoverable via .trash on desktop; the R4-F4 source-readiness check already guards the degraded/index-loss source case; the R2-F2 onGuard wiring makes a refusal visible). OPTIONS for the fix: (a) drop the empty-manifest override for a mount scope (empty subtree ≠ index loss) — converges but removes that index-loss belt for the mount; (b) scope-scale MIN/RATIO or add an absolute deletes>=MIN floor; (c) keep the conservative refuse+notify (current) and rely on remove+re-add to recover. discoveredInField=false (critique-found). Severity Medium (non-convergence of legit deletions + an under-protected tiny-mount drain; recoverable, gated by the readiness check + .trash + onGuard). RESOLVED by D0041 (bulkDeleteConfirm): the whole-vault ratio/empty heuristic is replaced by a user-configurable per-scope confirmation, so a small mount no longer false-fires and a legit bulk delete either applies below-threshold or is held for a one-click confirm.

rows.title: The wire-signature ENDPOINTS list is hand-maintained and the drift gate is generated FROM it, so it can silently diverge from the real axum router
rows.description: D0042 pre-ship critique finding F4 (MED). ENDPOINTS (server/src/wire_signature.rs) is a hand-written const; the CI drift gate committed_artifact_matches_generated only checks the committed JSON equals canonical_signature(), which is built FROM that same const — a tautology w.r.t. the router. Nothing cross-references ENDPOINTS against lib.rs build()'s actual routes. Consequence: remove a route but leave it in ENDPOINTS -> the signature still advertises it -> the client's diff sees it present -> proceeds -> the sync op 404s into a generic retry loop (the exact failure D0042 targets). Field-level TYPES are schemars-derived (safe); only the endpoint list is hand-maintained. FIX: a test that probes each ENDPOINTS path against the built router and asserts not-404 (405 method-mismatch is fine). discoveredInField=false (critique-found). Severity Medium (a future hand-maintenance drift, not a current defect; the list is correct today).

rows.title: The sync-mount push-back nudge makes a local delete propagate to a (possibly shared) source vault IMMEDIATELY, with no confirmation — needs an owner decision
rows.description: mountSyncPushLocal critique finding F1 (Medium, data-safety). The push-back nudge forces a full mount reconcile on a local file event, so a local delete under a SYNC-mount folder now propagates to the source PROMPTLY (before the fix it only propagated on the next reconnect). Deleting a folder locally deletes those files from the source server-side. This is CONSISTENT with D0041 (outgoing deletes are honored exactly, no bulk gate — owner decision) and receiving peers are still gated by THEIR incoming bulk-delete confirmation (D0041) before their local copies go — but the immediacy + the shared-source blast radius are new with this fix. Needs the owner to decide: accept as-is (record a Decision) OR add a confirmation for a mount outgoing delete-remote to a non-owned (shared) source over the bulk threshold. discoveredInField=false (critique-found). Severity Medium (a routine local reorganization promptly deletes from a shared vault; peers still gated on receive, and it is the owner's own action).

rows.title: Composed-mount path handling lacks sane defaults: source subfolder is unvalidated free text (though the folder set is knowable), and the local target folder is only created lazily so an empty/mistyped source never materializes it
rows.description: Owner field feedback on composed vaults. VERIFIED against code: (1) the add-mount source subfolder is a plain free-text input with NO existence check (mountsettings.ts:107-108); validateMounts only guards blank/.obsidian/overlap (mounts.ts:114-134). The source vault IS a real dropdown, but the subfolder within it is unconstrained. (2) The client CAN know the valid folders — a source-scoped changes(0) listing returns the file paths (transport.ts:271, mountio.ts:64) from which folders are derivable — but the mount UI never calls it, so a typo just pulls an empty set (and can trip the empty-subtree bulk-delete guard, main.ts:2257). (3) The local mount-point folder is created only LAZILY on the first file write (main.ts:251-252); if the source subtree is empty or mistyped, no write happens and the folder is never created. WANT: autofill/validate the source subfolder from the derived folder list so the user selects a KNOWN-VALID path; eagerly ensure the local mount point exists on add; warn/block a mount whose source matches nothing. CONFIRMED REPRO (2026-08-11, owner): a mount of source vault syncme subfolder B into vault asi (local syncme/B) did nothing — the source cursor advanced to v12 but base=0 because the B folder is EMPTY (syncme/A has notes, B has none), so the path filter matched zero files and the local syncme/B folder was never created; the owner got no feedback that B was empty or that 0 files matched (the path-filter code itself is correct). discoveredInField=true (owner). Severity Medium (silent empty pull + never-created folder + possible guard trip; recoverable).

rows.title: Composed mounts are ~60s poll-driven, not event-driven — they feel slow next to the WebSocket-instant primary vault
rows.description: Owner field report. The primary vault syncs via a WebSocket (instant), but composed mounts have no source subscription — pollMount runs on the ~60s primary poll cadence (mountsync.ts header + main.ts:2087 note it as a deferred D0039 refinement), so a source change can lag up to a minute. FIX: give each active mount a live subscription (a WS channel on the source vault, or a per-vault multiplex of the primary WS) so source changes pull promptly, keeping the poll as a backstop. discoveredInField=true (owner). Severity Low-Medium (latency/UX; correctness is unaffected — the poll still converges).

rows.title: A local edit to a read-only composed file (source unchanged) is kept on disk and only reported — it lingers as an un-syncable divergence that re-notifies every poll and never converges
rows.description: Owner asked what happens when RO is selected and the file is changed in the parent vault. VERIFIED: for a pull (read-only) mount, a local edit whose source is unchanged yields action push, which finalize turns into reportReadOnly (reconcile.ts:79-81) executed as onReadOnly only (reconcile.ts:1131-1133) — the edit is NOT pushed (RO honored), NOT reverted, NOT copied; it stays on disk as a silent local divergence, and every poll re-hits push->reportReadOnly (re-notify, never converge). A conflict copy is created only IF the source ALSO later diverges (planMerge readOnlyKeepCopy, reconcile.ts:118,953-961). This is a design characteristic, not a guarded bug. WANT: a defined, user-legible outcome for an edit on a RO mount (e.g. offer discard-my-edit or fork-to-a-writable-copy, or make the non-syncing state unmistakable) rather than a perpetual silent divergence. discoveredInField=true (owner). Severity Medium (the user may believe an edit synced when it silently will not).

rows.title: Client-consumed sharing/admin response shapes (SharedVault, VaultShares, ShareLinkInfo) are outside the 13-type signature map, so a breaking change to them is not caught
rows.description: D0042 pre-ship critique finding F5 (LOW-MED). The signature types map covers the 13 core protocol types but the client also consumes SharedVault (GET /api/shared, POST /api/share-redeem), VaultShares (GET /api/admin/vaults), and ShareLinkInfo (GET /api/share-links) — covered only at the endpoint level, not field-level, and these are as-cast in the client with NO validate guard (unlike the core types). A breaking rename/retype there (e.g. redeemed_by -> redeemedBy, expires_at number -> string) passes the signature diff untouched and is caught, if at all, only by absent/ad-hoc client parsing. Documented as v1 scope (wire_signature.rs scope note) but real. FIX: derive JsonSchema on these types + include them in the signature map (and add client-side validate for them). discoveredInField=false (critique-found). Severity Low-Medium (a breaking change to a secondary response shape is silently missed; the core sync/auth/status contract IS covered).

rows.title: The F2 bulk-push-to-shared guard reuses the incoming bulk-DELETE strategy/threshold, so turning that off (or a below-threshold pruned batch) leaves peer-deletion resurrection unguarded
rows.description: Independent critique of the F2 fix (MEDIUM). computeBulkPushHold reuses bulkDeleteStrategy/bulkDeleteThreshold. Two consequences: (1) a user who sets the INCOMING bulk-delete confirmation to 'off' ALSO silently disables the OUTGOING push-resurrection guard — one knob, two very different data-safety behaviors, no separate control or warning; with 'off' a base-loss re-first-contact with PRUNED tombstones resurrects the peer's whole deletion set. (2) Even with the guard on, a pruned-deletion batch that stays BELOW the threshold is pushed (resurrected) — inherent to a mass-only threshold. The LIVE-tombstone case is always safe (finalize keeps it local unconditionally); this is the no-tombstone/pruned residue only. The default is count/10 so out-of-the-box everyone is protected against a mass; only an explicit 'off' or a small pruned set is exposed. Also folds the LOW transient-changes(0)-under-report finding: a single-file transient tombstone omission at keep-time could stamp a base and later removeLocal — narrow and outside the trusted-server model (D0007). Robust fix: a DEDICATED push-guard control (or a hard floor independent of the delete knob), since it protects a PEER's data. discoveredInField=false. Severity Medium (peer-data resurrection when the shared knob is off / sub-threshold).

rows.title: A held-review resolver clears the WHOLE pending set (delete(scope)), so a deletion a reconcile ADDED while the resolver's task was queued silently vanishes from the review
rows.description: Concurrency-lens critique of the 1.29.x cluster (MEDIUM; worsened by the 1.29.1 serialization). acceptBulkDeletions/keepBulkDeletions + acceptBulkPushes/keepBulkPushes ran pendingBulk*.delete(scope) in their tail - clearing the ENTIRE scope, not the applied snapshot. Because the resolver's base mutation now DEFERS behind an in-flight reconcile (the engine task queue), that reconcile can setPendingBulk(authoritative) a NEW held path B before the tail runs, and the blanket delete(scope) then wipes B from the Conflicts review (B's toast already fired). B is NOT wrongly deleted (safe direction - never passed to io.remove), but it disappears from review until the next full scan (~15 min), a trust defect for a data-safety gate. FIX: clearHeldPaths subtracts ONLY the applied snapshot; a mid-resolve-added held path survives. discoveredInField=false. Severity Medium (review-surface data-integrity; no file loss).

rows.title: The provenance-column migration ran three autocommit ALTERs gated by a SINGLE-column probe — a crash between them permanently bricks the commit/delete path
rows.description: Mixed-fleet/migration-lens critique of the 1.29.x cluster (MEDIUM, F1). migrate() added the three author_* columns to `files` (v2) / `deletions` (v3) as three separate autocommit conn.execute ALTERs, gated by one probe on author_user. A crash between them (a rolling-redeploy SIGKILL, OOM, or power loss on consumer hardware - the case synchronous=FULL exists for) leaves author_user present + the other two missing, the single-column probe PERMANENTLY satisfied, schema_version stamped to CURRENT, and every commit/delete INSERT (which references all columns) 500'ing forever with 'no such column' and NO self-heal. FIX: ensure_provenance_columns adds each column under its OWN pragma_table_info probe (idempotent), so a partially-migrated table self-heals on the next open (migrate runs every open). Covers both files + deletions. discoveredInField=false. Severity Medium (rare crash window, but a permanently bricked vault needing manual DB surgery).

rows.title: The schema-downgrade 503 body (~276 chars) sat just under the client's 300-char plain-text cap with no test — a reword could silently re-hide the rollback as an opaque 'HTTP 503'
rows.description: Critique of 5effd75 (MEDIUM). The client (transport.ts errText) surfaces a server error body only when .length <= 300, else it shows the opaque 'HTTP 503' fallback. The schema-downgrade message was ~276 chars - 24 chars of headroom - and NOTHING tested the cross-language coupling (the Rust test even asserted the body was LONG). A future editor lengthening the message would keep all Rust tests green while silently reverting the rollback to an undiagnosable 503. FIX (server-only): shortened the body to ~190 chars, extracted it to a SCHEMA_DOWNGRADE_MSG const, and pinned its length (<= 260 chars) in the mapping test with a comment naming the client's 300-char errText cap both ways. discoveredInField=false. Severity Medium (would silently defeat the just-shipped self-diagnosing-rollback fix).

rows.title: A sync pass in progress made the conflict/config/switch modals unusable for minutes with no indication of the state or the reason - functions were unavailable invisibly
rows.description: Owner 2026-09-07, after the Resolve-conflicts modal sat on its placeholder for the whole 152 s first aliased pass: 'this state should be tracked and indicated somewhere. better transparency, especially if it affects availability of functions. maybe just grey out some options until actually ready, along with an indication as to why? state tracking'.
