The plugin knew it was busy - the status light said 'Connecting... checked 750/1420 files' - but no surface whose FUNCTION that state degraded said so: the conflict modal, the config-differences modal and the vault switcher all rendered their committing buttons as if ready while their own file reads queued behind the pass (on a large vault, minutes), so the user read 'broken' where the truth was 'busy, here is why, here is when'. Transparency defect on the plugin's irreversible controls. FIX (busyStateGating): busyState() as a pure projection + onBusyChange() subscription; busygate.ts mounts a reason banner and disables the committing buttons in the three modals until the plugin reports settled; the action handlers also refuse with the reason. discoveredInField = true. Severity Medium (no data at risk; availability of functions was invisible).

rows.title: The conflict diff DELETED ignored timestamp lines instead of masking their values, hiding that keeping the other version would destroy this device s created:/updated: lines
rows.description: Found when the owner used the new Copy button and pasted a real conflict back. The conflict diff rendered normalizedContent(), which DELETES an ignored timestamp line rather than neutralising it. That is right for a content-identity hash but wrong for a diff: when only one side HAS the line, removing it from both makes it invisible. In the reported file, `created: 2026-04-01T14:54` and `updated: 2026-06-08T09:40` existed only on the Windows copy, and the diff showed neither - so choosing 'Keep the other device's' would have deleted both lines with no indication whatsoever, on an irreversible either-side choice. Self-inflicted: shipped in 1.30.1 in response to the owner's own request to ignore timestamp fields in the diff, implemented by dropping the lines instead of masking their values, and it reintroduced exactly the hiding that the invisible-character work had argued against one layer up. FIXED with maskedForDisplay: the VALUE is masked, the LINE always survives, so an ignore-worthy value difference is still silent while a missing line is always visible. Applies to the clipboard report too, so copied text matches the screen. discoveredInField=true. Severity Medium (no automatic data loss, but it concealed the consequence of a manual irreversible choice - the user could have deleted their own creation date believing nothing was at stake).

rows.title: The conflict diff rendered visually-identical lines as a -/+ pair, so an irreversible either-side choice had nothing visible to choose between (trailing space, NBSP, zero-width, NFC/NFD)
rows.description: Owner field report while reviewing real conflicts: the diff showed 'a lot of pseudo changes', specifically a '- tagNames:' / '+ tagNames:' pair whose two lines were visually identical, with the reasonable question of whether encoding or CR/NL was to blame and the reasonable expectation that 'a good diff should be line-return agnostic'. Half right. Line endings were ALREADY handled - a probe confirms CRLF vs LF, a lone CR and trailing blank lines each yield zero changed lines - so EOL was never the cause. The actual causes are invisible characters: a trailing space or tab (Markdown's hard line break!), a tab-vs-spaces indent, a non-breaking space U+00A0 which renders exactly like a space, a zero-width space/joiner or BOM, or NFC-vs-NFD Unicode. The DEFECT was not that the diff detected these - they are real content - but that it rendered them INDISTINGUISHABLY, asking the user to make an irreversible either-side choice between two lines they had no way to tell apart. Fixed by revealing them with per-class markers on changed lines only, plus an explanatory line when every changed line is invisible-only, and explicitly NOT by ignoring them (ignoring a trailing double space would hide a Markdown line break and could discard the user's version). discoveredInField=true. Severity Medium (no data loss, but it made an irreversible decision unmakeable - the user could not see what they were choosing between).

rows.title: The conflict diff ran an unbounded O(n*m) LCS over a nested matrix, freezing the UI for seconds on a large note - 12k lines took 4.5s, on open AND after every resolve
rows.description: Owner field report: 'resolve conflicts is extremely slow'. unifiedLineDiff called lcsPairs (an O(n*m) DP allocating a NESTED (n+1)x(m+1) number matrix) on WHOLE notes with no size bound. merge3 has guarded the same function with MAX_MERGE_LINES=5000 since it was written; the diff view had no bound at all, and the 400-row display cap in renderDiff is applied AFTER the full diff is computed, so it saved nothing. Measured on a fast desktop for notes differing by ONE line: 200 lines 3ms, 500 7ms, 1k 32ms, 2k 89ms, 4k 447ms, 6k 1.06s, 8k 1.96s, 12k 4.5s - quadratic, on the UI thread, and run on modal open AND again after every single resolve. Mobile is several times slower again, and memory is the other half: 12k lines is 144M boxed cells. FIXED by stripping the common prefix/suffix before the DP (exact same output; a one-line edit collapses to 1x1) plus a 2,000,000-cell cap with a bounded whole-region fallback above it. Guarded by two perf assertions in merge.test.ts that FAILED first (3922ms and 404ms against a 250ms bound). discoveredInField=true.

rows.title: The conflict diff showed frontmatter timestamp fields the user had told SelfSync to ignore, so the modal contradicted its own setting
rows.description: Owner field report: 'doesn't seem to ignore metadata timestamp fields like it should in the diff view'. Correct - renderDiff passed RAW text to unifiedLineDiff, and noteconflict.ts imported nothing from frontmatter.ts. The ignore machinery (normalizedContent + reconcile's private ignorePatternsFor) was used ONLY by the sync engine, so the engine treated a timestamp-only change as no change while the modal drew it as a red/green changed line and asked the user to adjudicate it. FIXED with a new plugin.ignorePatternsForPath that mirrors reconcile's gating (feature on, .md, not .obsidian/ config where a `created:` must stay significant, not an excluded folder), passed into renderDiff, which now diffs normalizedContent of both sides - the masked lines are neither a change nor shown as context - and the no-changes message says so. The same identity now backs the stale-preview guard and the cosmetic auto-dismiss, so all three agree. discoveredInField=true.

rows.title: Resolve-conflicts modal: which side is − and which is + was fine print; the keep-buttons carried no sign
rows.description: Owner field report 2026-09-07 on the Resolve-conflicts modal: 'you say 'keep this device's' or keep the other's but you give no indication as to which one is − and which one is + in diff view. it should be concise and clear.' Cause: the only mapping from diff sign to side was an 11px, 70%-opacity legend line above the diff ('− the other version + this device's'), styled like fine print and worded differently from the buttons, while the two keep-buttons ('Keep the other device's' / 'Keep this device's') carried no sign at all - so a reader looking at red/green lines had to hunt for the mapping before an irreversible choice. Consequence: a user could keep the wrong side (data loss on the other device's edit) or stall on a conflict they could otherwise resolve in a second. Fix (conflictDiffSideLegend): the header names the mapping in words, the legend is two bold spans in the diff's own red/green with the signs, and the buttons carry the signs ('Keep − other device's' / 'Keep + this device's'). Guarded by a DOM test. discoveredInField = true. Severity Medium (a UX defect on the one irreversible control in the plugin).

rows.title: The conflict modal read EVERY conflicting file pair serially before drawing anything, so opening it cost ~2N disk round-trips to display ONE conflict
rows.description: Owner field report: 'resolve conflicts is extremely slow' (the open, distinct from the diff freeze). run() executed the whole cosmetic auto-dismiss sweep BEFORE the first render: for every conflict, two STRICTLY SEQUENTIAL adapter.readBinary calls plus FOUR full UTF-8 decodes (isMergeable on each side, then sameIgnoringEol decoding both again) and two regex passes over the full text - all behind a 'Checking conflicts...' placeholder, and all repeated on every open. The modal only ever displays ONE conflict, so none of that work was needed to paint. FIXED by rendering first and sweeping in the background (redrawing only if something was dismissed), gating on the free extension check BEFORE any read so a binary attachment costs zero IO, decoding each side once with a strict fatal decode, and running the sweep at concurrency 8. Guarded by DOM tests that hang readBytesOrNull forever and still expect a painted conflict, and that assert a .png conflict performs zero reads. Related and fixed alongside: issueConflictResolveRepaintsPerFile (a settings repaint + whole-vault getFiles per resolved file) and issueConflictModalDoubleApply (unawaited render with no re-entry guard on an irreversible choice). discoveredInField=true.

rows.title: Note content identity does not Unicode-normalise, so NFC vs NFD text that renders identically counts as a divergence - a latent phantom-conflict generator for cross-platform vaults
rows.description: Found while diagnosing issueConflictDiffInvisibleChars. Note CONTENT identity does not Unicode-normalise at ALL: grep shows normalize("NF...") appears exactly once in client/src, at mounts.ts canonSeg, and that is for mount folder PATHS - never for content. normalizedContent (and therefore normalizedHash, the sync engine's content-identity hash) compares NFC and NFD forms of the same text as DIFFERENT. Consequence: text that is canonically equivalent and renders identically - the classic case being 'cafe' with a precomposed e-acute versus e plus a combining acute - is treated as a genuine divergence. macOS has historically produced decomposed (NFD) forms where Windows and Android produce NFC, and SelfSync explicitly targets desktop-plus-mobile cross-platform vaults, so a vault spanning a Mac and a PC can generate conflict copies for notes nobody edited, repeatedly, with a diff whose two sides look identical. NOT FIXED HERE, deliberately: changing content identity changes what the sync engine considers the same file, so it needs its own pass with care over the base-hash migration (every stored normHash would shift), whether to normalise on write or only on compare, and mobile performance of normalising large notes. The conflict UI now at least TELLS the user the two versions are visually identical (invisibleOnlyDifference NFC-folds before comparing), so the symptom is explicable rather than baffling. Needs: a decision on normalise-on-compare vs normalise-on-write, a migration plan for stored hashes, and a test with real NFD content from a Mac. discoveredInField=false (found by instrumentation; the field symptom it would cause is exactly the phantom-conflict class already reported). Severity Medium (latent phantom-conflict generator for any non-ASCII text in a cross-platform vault; no data loss - a conflict copy keeps both sides).

rows.title: Nothing re-examined existing conflict copies - not on load, not in reconcile - so an already-CONVERGED conflict stayed in the count until someone opened the modal, behaving exactly like a stale flag
rows.description: Owner question: 'i'm not sure if refreshing the plugin autoresolves as much as it can and this is a genuine outstanding issue, or if it was just flagged as an issue and isn't being reanalyzed on a plugin update as it should. which is it?' Investigated; the answer is both-and-neither, and there IS a defect. NOT a stale flag: a note conflict is DERIVED from a conflict-copy FILE on disk, and listNoteConflicts recomputes it from vault.getFiles() on every call (D-conflict-model), so the count cannot drift from reality. THE DEFECT: refreshing the plugin auto-resolved nothing at all. The cosmetic sweep was invoked from exactly ONE place - NoteConflictModal.run() - and nothing else in the codebase ever re-examined an existing conflict copy: not onload, not reconcileAll, not reconcilePath. reconcile CREATES copies and treats an existing one as a plain file thereafter. So a conflict whose two sides had since CONVERGED - identical content, or differing only in line endings or in frontmatter timestamp keys the user chose to ignore - stayed in the count indefinitely, and then disappeared the instant someone opened the modal. That behaviour is indistinguishable from a stale flag being cleared, which is exactly why it was reported as one. FIXED by moving the sweep to the plugin (dismissCosmeticConflicts) and running it once per load from onLayoutReady, so a refresh really does auto-resolve everything it safely can; the modal delegates and passes its open flag so closing it cancels the background work. Safe by construction: a copy is only deleted when content identity says the sides are the same, and binary/invalid-UTF-8 pairs are excluded before any read. discoveredInField=true. Severity Medium (no data loss, but the conflict count overstated real outstanding work indefinitely, and the disappear-on-open behaviour actively undermined trust in the count).

rows.title: real-Obsidian e2e ran green on Obsidian 1.5.8, below the plugin's minAppVersion 1.11.0 - a green run outside the supported envelope proves nothing
rows.description: Found 2026-09-07 while trying to automate l3GuiPass (the manual GUI pass) as a real-Obsidian Playwright demonstration. The machine's Obsidian is 1.5.8 (Electron 28 / Chrome 120); manifest.json declares minAppVersion 1.11.0, and client/src/settings.ts imports SettingGroup from the obsidian API, which 1.5.8 does not provide. The e2e-obsidian suite (smoke, configsync, convergence) nevertheless ran GREEN on 1.5.8 this sitting, because those specs only load the plugin and sync files - they never open the settings tab. So the layer that exists to prove the real glue works was proving it on an Obsidian no user of this plugin can run (Obsidian refuses to enable a plugin below minAppVersion), and the first spec to touch the settings UI would have failed for a reason unrelated to the plugin. Hazard class: a test environment silently outside the supported envelope - green means nothing, red means noise. FIX (e2eObsidianVersionGate): obsidianDriver reads the running version from the renderer user agent and every spec skips loudly, naming installed vs. minimum, when the install is below the floor. The operator-facing consequence is honest: on this machine the real-Obsidian layer now SKIPS until Obsidian is updated to >= 1.11.0 - which is also what l3GuiPass needs before it can be demonstrated. discoveredInField = false. Severity Medium (assurance defect, no data at risk).

rows.title: The .engine/ tree is a 6-week-stale vintage against the keel binary that gates commits - four guards fail under keel 0.3.1, and every recent keel-guard-ALL-PASS record was a stale sibling build verdict
rows.description: Surfaced the instant a real pre-commit gate ran for the first time. TWO compounding causes: no git hook was installed at all (issueHooksNotInstalled), and CLAUDE.md section 5 documented the validator as a local Windows release-build path that does NOT exist in this repo - so a 6-week-old sibling checkout's keel was run by hand instead of the keel 0.3.1 on PATH. Consequence: engine drift accumulated unseen, and the keel verdicts recorded in D0046 and the provenanceDecoupling DoD were that stale binary's - both records now carry an explicit GATE CORRECTION rather than being rewritten. Under 0.3.1: viewpoint-renderer 9 violations (declared renderers name commands 0.3.1 does not expose - and CLAUDE.md section 1 documents those same commands, so the doc surface is stale too); cli-surface-declared 1 (.engine/cli/commands.sysml absent, keel migrate resyncs); tool-reference 1 (engine-triage/SKILL.md references a non-existent .engine/tools/triage_reminder.py); sprint-closure 1 (tracked as issueMootedTaskUnstamped); plus 19 unread warnings. A keel migrate --dry-run reports 481 .engine/ files, 0 blockers, nothing outside .engine/. NOT run: a 481-file process/schema-definition change needs owner acceptance + a co-committed Decision (D0070 keystone). BLOCKS ALL COMMITS meanwhile. The recurrence guard is already structurally in place - the installed pre-commit hook invokes plain keel, so the real gate can no longer be sidestepped by reaching for a stale build - plus CLAUDE.md now says to check keel --version first. discoveredInField=false. Severity Medium (no user impact; a silently-drifted commit gate and overstated verification records).

rows.title: Two real-Obsidian e2e helpers ARE derived from vrtmrz/obsidian-livesync (authored by vorotamoroz, confirmed) and carry no upstream MIT notice — the only remaining upstream code in the repo
rows.description: Found by a complete livesync-reference audit after an earlier truncated (head -40) sweep missed it. client/e2e-obsidian/helpers/obsidian.ts and helpers/obsidianFunctions.ts both self-declare 'Ported from origin/test_real_obsidian'; authorship was CONFIRMED against the leftover fork's test_real_obsidian branch — test_e2e/helpers/obsidian.ts and obsidianFunctions.ts were authored by vorotamoroz on 2026-05-11 and 2026-05-14, before this project existed (2026-07-04). Measured overlap, whitespace/comments normalized: obsidian.ts 55 of our 111 code lines identical to upstream's 137, including the whole waitForCDP(port, timeoutMs) signature and the CDP poll/attach sequence; obsidianFunctions.ts 8 of 15, including the global app plugin-registry type declaration. Punctuation-only lines inflate that somewhat, but the signatures and the type shape are substantive: this is derived work, and upstream is MIT, so its notice-retention obligation applies to these two files. This CORRECTS an earlier same-sitting claim that HEAD's tree held no upstream source — that check was filename- and dependency-based and missed a file whose own header declared the derivation. Scope limits worth keeping straight: NEITHER file is bundled into the built plugin (e2e tooling only), so nothing SHIPPED to users contains upstream code; both are distributed in repo source. Resolution needs an OWNER DECISION between (A) attribute — add upstream's MIT notice to the two files or a NOTICE naming them — and (B) re-implement both helpers independently and drop the ported-from claims, which is the complete decoupling the owner asked for. Also gates a README wording review: D0046's no-shared-code statement is true of the plugin and server but not of these two helpers. discoveredInField=false. Severity Medium (licence-compliance + a provenance claim that is currently overbroad; no user-facing or security impact).

rows.title: Content identity does not trim trailing whitespace inside frontmatter, so two devices whose plugin versions serialise an empty YAML value differently regenerate the SAME conflict forever
rows.description: Diagnosed from the owner's pasted conflict; NOT fixed, and deliberately so. The six differing frontmatter lines differ ONLY by a trailing space: the other device writes `tagNames: `, `filesPaths: `, `bookmarksGroups: `, `excludes: `, `extends: `, `favoriteView: ` with a trailing space for the empty value, and this device writes them without. In YAML both forms are the same null value, so the two files are semantically identical on those lines. The shape of the file (fields / valuesList / fieldsOrder / mapWithTag) is a Metadata Menu fileClass, so the likely source is two different plugin or Obsidian versions serialising an empty value differently on the two devices. normalizedContent normalises EOL and BOM and masks ignored timestamp keys, but does NOT trim trailing whitespace, so content identity treats these as genuinely divergent - which means every time either device rewrites that file the conflict is regenerated. This is a permanent conflict LOOP, not a one-off, and it is the actual reason the owner keeps seeing conflicts on this note. WHY NOT FIXED HERE: the fix is to trim trailing whitespace on lines INSIDE the frontmatter fences in normalizedContent - safe in YAML, and body lines must stay untouched because in Markdown two trailing spaces are a hard line break. But normalizedContent feeds normalizedHash, so changing it shifts every stored normHash; a persisted hash computed under the old algorithm would no longer match a freshly computed one, which can make files look changed once and generate exactly the conflict copies being eliminated. That needs a migration decision (recompute-and-restamp on load, or grandfather stored hashes, or compare-both-ways during a transition), which is the same class of change as issueContentIdentityNotUnicodeNormalised and belongs with it. Interim behaviour is honest: the diff now reveals the trailing spaces as middle dots and states that the versions differ only in invisible characters. discoveredInField=true. Severity Medium (recurring phantom conflicts on any note a differently-versioned plugin rewrites; no data loss, but persistent noise and a standing risk of the user resolving in the wrong direction).

rows.title: 103 delivery DoDs (80 method=test) read DONE in prose but carry no TestResult - shipped work with unrecorded verdicts; blocks honest #Verify edges for sr11/sr16/sr19
rows.description: Found 2026-09-07 while authoring #Verify edges from Tests to the 25 STPA SafetyRequirements. A census of .tracking/delivery/delivery.sysml shows 103 verification Tests (DoDs) with no TestResult of any kind: 80 method=test, 14 inspect, 3 demo, 1 analyze, 1 critique, 4 confirmation. Their action comments and procedure texts read DONE and name the releases they shipped in (m1ProtocolDoD .. round7RecoveryFixesDoD, autoReindexDoD, uiFunctionalAuditDoD, round1DeferredHardeningDoD and others), and .tracking/verification/acceptance.sysml adds 5 unstamped method=test acceptance Tests for the embedded-timestamp requirements that timestampIgnoreRedesign (1.9.0) retired. CONSEQUENCE: (a) three SafetyRequirements (sr11 refuse-reindex-over-incomplete-directory, sr16 operator-repair-any-vault, sr19 bound-uncommitted-storage) cannot honestly carry a #Verify edge although the verifying server tests exist and pass - the DoD that owns each was never stamped; (b) every computed lens that keys on recorded verdicts (assured, tier-satisfaction, sitting-coverage, whats-next) under-reports work that shipped, while the prose over-reports it - the exact drift CLAUDE.md 2.1 exists to prevent (prose is not truth; the verdict is). WHY IT HAPPENED: these DoDs predate the write-API (2026-06-15) becoming the primary path and the evidence-cited convention (2026-08-25); DONE was written into the comment and the result never appended. Not fabricated here: a pass without a receipt would be a testimony, not a record (D0232). RESOLVER: dodBackfillStamp - classify each as reproducible (stamp at HEAD with a real run receipt), mooted (record the superseding decision as basis), or owner-judgment (listed for the owner), with reconciled control totals (D0067). discoveredInField = false. Severity Medium: no data at risk, but the record's honesty is the deliverable of this engine.

rows.title: No git hook ran in this repo at all — a machine-global core.hooksPath pointed at a non-existent directory, silently disabling the pre-commit keel gate as well as the push, while CLAUDE.md asserted the push hook was running
rows.description: Found when a commit during the provenance decoupling did not auto-push. core.hooksPath was set machine-globally (file:C:/Users/will/.gitconfig) to ~/.githooks, which DOES NOT EXIST; git silently runs NO hooks when hooksPath names a missing directory. So the repo's own .githooks/pre-commit — the keel validate + keel guard commit gate — had never fired either, and .git/hooks held no non-sample hook. Separately there was no post-commit hook in the repo at all, yet CLAUDE.md 4 asserted 'the post-commit hook pushes every commit' — a doc claiming a control that did not exist, which is worse than a missing control because it stops anyone looking for it. The two commits made before the fix were gated manually instead (keel validate + guard run by hand, green both times) so nothing unvalidated landed, but that was vigilance, not a control. FIXED in-pass (see hooksInstall). RESIDUAL, out of this repo's scope and reported to the owner: the machine-global core.hooksPath is still broken, so every OTHER repo on this workstation remains hook-less. discoveredInField=false. Severity Medium (a silently-disabled commit gate — the class of failure that lets an invalid commit land unnoticed).

rows.title: keel-parser silently skips the 74 nested #Covers edges inside action def SelfSyncDelivery - sitting-coverage read 0 covered against 74 authored covering edges
Every settings re-render ran a recursive filesystem walk per synced plugin, so ONE conflict-resolve click cost a walk per plugin - seconds on Windows or a cloud-synced vault, regardless of note size
rows.description: THE defect that actually explains the owner's observation, found only after they pushed back: 'the diffs i was seeing were only on ~100 line files, but still took > 6 seconds or so'. At ~100 lines the LCS diff costs about 3ms (measured), so the quadratic-diff defect - real, and fixed - could NOT be the reported symptom; the AI's first explanation over-weighted it. The cost that fits scales with the number of SYNCED PLUGINS and the filesystem, not with note length. settings.ts renderPluginChecklist called plugin.pluginSyncClean(id) for EVERY synced plugin on EVERY render, UNCONDITIONALLY - even on the line right after the cached answer had already been applied - and pluginSyncClean runs walkConfigTree, a RECURSIVE adapter.list/stat walk over .obsidian/plugins/<id>. So any settings re-render cost one full filesystem walk per synced plugin. resolveNoteConflict ends by calling settingsRefresh, which IS a full settings display(), so a SINGLE 'Keep this device's' click paid for a walk per plugin; with ~10 synced plugins on Windows (antivirus on every stat) or a cloud-synced vault (placeholder hydration), that is seconds per click. It also compounded the modal OPEN: the old pre-render cosmetic sweep called resolveNoteConflict once per dismissed file, so N cosmetic conflicts meant N settings rebuilds, each doing that per-plugin walk plus a whole-vault vault.getFiles(). FIXED by walking ONLY when the answer is not cached; the cache is already invalidated where it matters (deleted per-plugin after a push/pull changes convergence, cleared wholesale on hide() so re-opening the tab re-checks), and staleness within one tab session errs safe - a button left live is a guarded no-op, never a wrong action. This is the fix for the single-click apply; the separate coalescing of settingsRefresh (issueConflictResolveRepaintsPerFile) only ever helped the BATCH case and would not have fixed one click. Guarded fail-first: with two synced plugins and three renders the guard saw 6 walks before the fix and 2 after. discoveredInField=true. Severity Medium (no data risk; a multi-second UI stall on an ordinary action).

rows.title: The sync engine's EngineState is the one hazard-bearing state machine not on the shared fsm.ts primitive - no explicit table, STPA registration pending
rows.description: Found 2026-09-08 while putting every hazard-bearing state machine on the shared fsm.ts primitive (owner: 'FSM module, used all across the project in places where states that can introduce hazards exist'). Four of five machines moved cleanly because they were already pure reducers (connstate linkNext, mountfsm, transportstate, resolvefsm). The fifth - the sync engine's EngineState in syncengine.ts, the controller c2SyncEngine's own phase and the most hazard-bearing state in the client (H-6 unavailability, H-9 reported state vs actual, H-10 ceasing recovery) - keeps its transitions as class-internal setState() calls interleaved with effects, so there is no rule table to prove total, no tableCoverage, and the STPA registration is STPA-FSM-PENDING. Not a defect in behaviour (syncengine.test covers the paths that exist) but a gap in the property the FSM discipline exists to give: that every hazard-bearing transition is enumerable and analysed. Resolver engineFsmOnPrimitive. discoveredInField = false. Severity Medium.

rows.title: Preserving both versions of a conflict required the slow editor merge - there was no one-press 'keep both'
rows.description: Owner 2026-09-08: 'open both to merge is so incredibly slow... maybe just keep both that auto keeps both content? i don't want to open it up and merge all the time, most of the time i just want to preserve data'. The modal offered three outcomes - discard the other device's version, discard this device's version, or hand-merge in the editor - so the most common intent, 'lose nothing, decide later', was only reachable through the slowest path (opening both files as editor panes) or by leaving the conflict unresolved. FIX (keepBothResolution): 'Keep both' - one press turns the conflict copy into an ordinary note beside the original ('<name> (this device's version <date>)'), both sync, the conflict ends, nothing is merged by hand; first among the choices; 'Open both to merge' kept last. discoveredInField = true. Severity Medium (UX: the safe outcome was the expensive one).

rows.title: Resolving a conflict dimmed the whole modal with no state - working, hung or done were indistinguishable, and the upload it triggers was invisible
rows.description: Owner 2026-09-08: 'give me a state machine during resolution, like updating server... or something. can't just gray the modal on me. UX'. Pressing Keep in the Resolve-conflicts modal dimmed the whole body (opacity .55, pointer-events none) until resolveNoteConflict returned: on a large vault that is a preview re-check, a read, a write and a delete - plus an enqueued upload the modal did not wait for - with the only signal being a greyed screen. The user could not tell whether it was working, hung, or done, and the upload the resolution actually triggers was invisible entirely. Same class as issueBusyStateNotSurfaced (functions in a state the surface did not show), on the one irreversible control. FIX (resolutionStateMachine): the pressed button narrates the plugin's real steps via onStage and then 'Updating the server…' until the engine settles (bounded); the other keep-button disabled, Copy/Close live, no dimming. discoveredInField = true. Severity Medium.

rows.title: Published plugin assets are checked for presence, never for integrity
rows.description: Found by the STPA over the release-channel authority (2026-09-10, UCA-58 / SR-50 in .tracking/safety/stpa-authorities.sysml). check-release.mjs and verify-released.yml assert that the manifest version is tagged, published and carries the BRAT assets, and check-release-currency bounds unreleased drift, but nothing attests that the published main.js is the CI build of the tagged commit: no recorded digest, no signature, no post-publish comparison. A replaced or corrupted asset installs through BRAT on every device unnoticed (H-5). Non-trivial: touches release.yml, the release script and the plugin's About surface; signing is a separate owner decision.

rows.title: No coexistence rule for another sync tool operating on the same directory
rows.description: Found by the STPA over the same-device authorities (2026-09-10, UCA-52 / SR-47 in .tracking/safety/stpa-authorities.sysml). Step 1 recorded 'other sync tools' as an authority present in the owner's own vault (`.sync-conflict-*` files exist there), but the plugin has no coexistence rule: it neither detects a co-located tool nor recognises that tool's artefacts, so another tool's conflict copies sync everywhere as authored content, and two tools rewriting one file have nothing bounding the loop (the plugin bounds only the echo of its own writes). Hazard H-13 (another same-device authority) and H-6 (a rewrite loop starves real changes). Non-trivial: needs an owner call on whether foreign conflict copies are skipped or synced, and a loop breaker with a threshold.

rows.title: The 1.30.17 coexistence code froze the skip setting in mount scopes and let a user release disarm the loop breaker permanently
rows.description: Panel 2026-09-11 (other-sync-tools critic, FT1..FT8; identity critic ID3): the mount runtime captured skipForeignArtefacts as a boolean while the mount io read the live setting — a mid-session toggle could tombstone a based foreign path on the SOURCE; 'Upload current versions anyway' set a standing override so the loop resumed unbounded with the row hidden; the default limit misclassified a person toggling a checkbox; foreign paths already on the server were reported as 'config files'; root-marker detection was unreachable (the host never indexes dot paths); toggling the skip off did not resync; the loop breaker did not reach mounts or the merged-push site. Resolver: sprint coexistenceHardening.

rows.title: Content identity is one-sided and its seam / adopt paths can still spawn phantom copies or drop invisible content
rows.description: Panel 2026-09-11 (identity critic, ID1/ID2/ID4/ID5/ID6/ID8): the push→in-sync override stamps the scan-skip hint on a raw-different file and the write seam then copies a stamp-only local on a remote move (UCA-49 'closed' only in the single-sided case); a 'merge' with one cosmetically-changed side conflicts instead of pulling/pushing; adopt-remote drops a masked timestamp line present on one side only; in-fence trimming reaches YAML block scalars; the display does not fold what identity folds; hot-load is keyed on the vault being private now, not on who wrote the code (a peer's main.js under a since-revoked grant executes). Resolver: sprint contentIdentityTwoSided.

rows.title: Primary base entries freeze under a mounted folder and drive silent overwrites / delete-remotes on unmount
rows.description: Panel 2026-09-11 (composed-vaults critic, CV1..CV5): (1) while a folder is mounted the primary skips it, so its base entries there keep pre-mount values; on remove the primary pushes the mount's content over its own copy with no conflict copy and delete-remotes what the mount removed — fleet-wide (H-1, H-14). (2) Renaming the mount-point folder left the mount localGone while the primary uploaded the peer's whole subtree into the user's vault. (3) A note dragged into a pull mount is tombstoned on the primary and stranded, with a misleading toast. (4) The source grant is read once per connect, so a mid-session downgrade leaves a Sync mount 'In sync' while every push 403s. (5) Four mount lifecycle writes bypass mountMachine (SR-36 false). Resolver: sprint mountScopeBoundaryHardening.

rows.title: The safety model's claims drifted from the code: SR-5 false, six #Verify edges that verify nothing, unanalysed control actions, an unmodelled operator prune, stale prose
rows.description: Panel 2026-09-11 (SE critic, SE1..SE7; identity ID7; release RL3): SR-5 stated 'never, for ANY vault' against shipped hot-load; six #Verify edges cite DoDs that do not exercise the SR; eight control actions had no UCA and c1User none; POST /api/admin/prune-history destroys SR-1's evidence with no ControlAction/UCA/SR; the D0041 incoming mass-deletion hold was load-bearing but unstated; pmSyncEngine beliefs omitted the terminal `unloading` state and the header still said PENDING; c15ReleaseChannel realizes SRs while declared uncommandable; cc49 and cc55/sr50 over-claimed. Resolver: sprint stpaModelHonesty.
